rubric.scope: Private defense technology companies raising $500K-$15M (with tolerance band to $16.5M)
rubric.not_for: Due diligence, portfolio management, technical merit evaluation

section.name: Evaluation Context
section.block: This is a two-profile Ideal Company Profile (ICP) scoring instrument built for a fundraiser to use as a top-of-funnel qualification and prioritization tool. Its purpose is to evaluate private defense technology companies (defense-AI, autonomous systems, cybersecurity, counter-UAS, space/ISR, maritime autonomy, hypersonics/directed energy, defense electronics, and dual-use technology) that are actively seeking capital in the $500K-$15M range and produce a structured, scored assessment of each company's probability of successfully closing a funding round. This instrument is not a due diligence tool and was not designed for technical merit evaluation or investment decision-making. It scores fundraising velocity and investor appetite, not technical promise, mission importance, national-security relevance, or engineering merit.

The rubric is explicitly built to identify companies that can raise money most easily - not companies with the best technology, the most important mission, or the greatest national-security value. Technical promise and fundraising ease diverge meaningfully in practice. The evaluation target is investor psychology, deal velocity, and capital market dynamics. Every criterion, weight, and scoring band is calibrated against this objective. STANDING INSTRUCTION: The objective is fundraising velocity and investor appetite - not technical promise, mission importance, or national-security relevance. Score accordingly.

block.name: Client Specifications
block.spec: Series A (100%), Seed/Pre-Seed+ (85%), Pre-Seed below $500K with no institutional participation (excluded)

Single most important criterion at Profile B. Strong preference for defense halo-employer alumni (Anduril, Palantir, SpaceX, Shield AI, DARPA, DIU, IC/SOF pedigree), complementary technical-plus-operational founding pairs, and demonstrated development capacity. Solo founders accepted with profile-specific protocol per C1. Advisor-heavy / engineering-light teams ("Fool's Gold") are penalized.

Sporadic, messy, or structurally compromised cap tables are a hard disqualifier. Unmitigated CFIUS/FOCI exposure, IP not assigned, stacked SAFEs above $3M with no priced round, and founder ownership below threshold are additional hard disqualifiers per Section 2.3.
US-primary (DoD, CFIUS, SBIR/STTR, DIU, DARPA as primary reference frame); globally applicable.
Government program relationships, CVC validation, and prime-contractor relationships preferred but not a hard requirement.

Defense-appropriate expectations: patents weighted at zero for software-primary defense companies; patents add modest positive signal for hardware-intensive companies; ITAR/EAR-protected know-how and classified approaches treated via Information Scarcity Protocol (Section 1.5). Moat-buildability trajectory (platform lock-in, manufacturing throughput, sole-source positioning) replaces patent moat as the primary defensibility signal.

section.block: The $500K-$15M range is split into Profile B (Seed, $500K-$3M) and Profile A (Series A, $3M-$15M) to create meaningful separation between two genuinely different fundraising environments. Because no universal regulatory stage applies across defense technology companies, the instrument uses three routing inputs simultaneously: (1) raise size, (2) development stage selected from the Defense Development Stage Taxonomy (DDST) in Section 2.1, and (3) investor composition characterized by the four-tier classification in Section 5 Block 1. The DDST serves the dual function that FDA regulatory stage serves in LS v5.1 - it anchors routing logic AND product-maturity signal context - and is operationalized in Section 2.1 and applied through the Product, Traction and Government Demand criterion (C3/A3/B3).

block.name: Information Scarcity Protocol
block.status: Carried from Tech ICP v1.0 with defense-specific content

section.block:
Two-track INFORMATION-SCARCE vs. INFORMATION-ABSENT classification carried from Tech ICP v1.0 (originally LS v5.1 v5.0 R4) with mechanism preserved exactly. Defense-specific observable-signal lists (research Workstream 4; PCDB DS-12A, DS-4) replace the tech signal lists. Two defense-specific named sub-protocols are added inside this block: the Classified-Program SCARCE Protocol (PCDB DS-12A) and the Stealth-Company Protocol (PCDB DS-12E). The "highest-predictive, lowest-observable" problem is acute in defense because key signals (classified programs, ITAR-controlled details, clearance specifics, contract-vehicle terms) are structurally non-public; the Classified-Program SCARCE Protocol governs every midpoint-default applied in a classified context. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE for the defense-specific signal lists and the one-artifact SCARCE standard - additional cases are needed to validate that the SCARCE/ABSENT distinctions function correctly across the defense business models the rubric covers.
When information for a criterion is insufficient to produce a confident score, assign the midpoint of the applicable scoring band and flag the score with [INSUFFICIENT DATA]. Do not penalize companies for missing information below the midpoint. This protocol applies to all criteria in both profiles. The Data Confidence indicator in Section 5 aggregates these flags to provide an overall assessment of score reliability.
MIDPOINT-DEFAULT JUSTIFICATION STANDARD: When the midpoint-default is applied to a criterion, the Justification field must do more than cite protocol application. The evaluator must articulate why the midpoint - rather than a score above or below midpoint within the band - is appropriate given whatever partial evidence exists. If partial evidence supports a score above or below the midpoint, score accordingly and document the partial evidence. Reserve the exact midpoint for situations where evidence is genuinely absent and no directional signal is available.
INFORMATION-SCARCE vs. INFORMATION-ABSENT CLASSIFICATION:
Before applying the midpoint-default to any criterion, the evaluator must classify the missing information as one of two types:
INFORMATION-SCARCE: Evidence exists that the company has engaged in the activity measured by this criterion, but the details are not publicly disclosed. The existence of the underlying activity is supported by some observable signal, even if specifics are not available. When information is SCARCE: apply the midpoint-default. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA - INFORMATION-SCARCE]. In the Justification field, state the observable signal that confirms the underlying activity exists.
INFORMATION-ABSENT: No evidence exists that the company has engaged in the activity measured by this criterion. The absence is not caused by non-disclosure of existing information but by the non-existence of the things the information would describe. When information is ABSENT: score in the lowest applicable band per the band definitions. The midpoint-default does not apply. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA - INFORMATION-ABSENT] and document in the Justification field: (a) what evidence was searched for, (b) why the absence is classified as information-absent rather than information-scarce, and (c) the specific band assigned and its justification.
AMBIGUOUS CASES: When partial evidence exists but it is ambiguous whether the underlying activity has occurred, default to INFORMATION-SCARCE and document the ambiguity. The INFORMATION-ABSENT classification should only be applied when the evaluator has actively searched for evidence of the underlying activity across available sources and found none.
DEFENSE-SPECIFIC OBSERVABLE SIGNALS - INFORMATION-SCARCE (activity exists but details not disclosed): C1 Team: Founder has confirmed employment history with any defense halo employer or government institution; LinkedIn shows active history; product exists implying a team built it; clearance/FCL signals in bios. C2 Sector: Company has a website or SAM.gov registration; product addresses an identifiable defense sub-sector. C3 Traction: Any SBIR.gov record; any USASpending.gov obligation; DIU/AFWERX press release; press release referencing "undisclosed government customer" with independent corroboration; exercise/demo announcement. C4 Government Access: SAM.gov entity registration; FCL in disclosed bios; reference to ATO/IL process in press; ITAR/EAR registration where product plainly requires it. C5 Cap Table: Investor names disclosed on Crunchbase/PitchBook; accelerator membership disclosed; round structure inferable from Crunchbase. C6 Capital Efficiency: UNDERLYING-ACTIVITY DEFINITION - the activity C6 measures is CAPITAL DEPLOYMENT (the conversion of capital into operations), not fundraising events. INFORMATION-SCARCE when corroborated deployment evidence exists alongside undisclosed financing: a shipped or demonstrated prototype, a named operating team, or observable operations each corroborates that capital is being deployed while round sizes and capital history remain undisclosed. Also SCARCE on partial financial signals: round size disclosed; employee count observable (LinkedIn); time since last round known; SBIR/STTR award amounts on SBIR.gov. C7 Position and Exit: Sub-sector inferable; acquirer universe assessable from named defense M&A activity.
DEFENSE-SPECIFIC TRIGGER CONDITIONS - INFORMATION-ABSENT (underlying activity does not exist): C1 Team: No employees confirmed on LinkedIn; founder identity uncorroborated by third-party sources; advisor-only "team" with no confirmed FTEs. C2 Sector: No website or SAM.gov registration; no product description in any public source. C3 Traction: No SBIR.gov record; no USASpending obligations; no press coverage of any government engagement; no prototype references in any source. C4 Government Access: No SAM.gov registration; no clearance or FCL signals; no vehicle evidence; no ITAR/EAR registration where product plainly requires it. C5 Cap Table: No investor names disclosed and no founder attestation possible (company has no investors). C6 Capital Efficiency: INFORMATION-ABSENT only when NO corroborated capital-deployment evidence exists - no fundraising disclosed, no documented capital history, AND no deployment corroboration (no shipped or demonstrated prototype, no named operating team, no observable operations). A zero-disclosure company WITH corroborated deployment evidence is INFORMATION-SCARCE (midpoint track), not ABSENT. C7 Position and Exit: Sub-sector so novel no acquirer universe can be defined (rare).
CLASSIFIED-PROGRAM SCARCE PROTOCOL: When a company's claimed activity involves classified programs, ITAR-controlled technical details, or security-clearance specifics, the evaluator must classify the information scarcity as follows before applying any midpoint default:
INFORMATION-SCARCE (justified midpoint default applies): At least ONE of the following corroborating public artifacts is present: (a) a USASpending.gov or SAM.gov obligation to a known or classified program office; (b) a press release referencing an "undisclosed government customer" that is independently corroborated by a second source; (c) company bios referencing active security clearances and/or a Facility Clearance (FCL); (d) named cleared personnel listed on the company's team page or in a press release. When information is SCARCE under this protocol, apply the midpoint default. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA - INFORMATION-SCARCE - CLASSIFIED-PROGRAM]. The Justification field MUST name the specific corroborating artifact. A bare mid-point invocation citing only "classified program" without naming the artifact is a format error.
INFORMATION-ABSENT (lowest band; midpoint default does NOT apply): No footprint exists on either the public-facing side OR the government-facing side - no SBIR.gov record, no USASpending obligations, no program mention in any source, no clearance or FCL signal, only a bare claim of classified work with no corroboration. Score in the lowest applicable band. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA - INFORMATION-ABSENT]. Document in the Justification: (a) what was searched, (b) why the absence is classified as ABSENT rather than SCARCE, and (c) the specific band assigned.
AMBIGUOUS CASES: Default to INFORMATION-SCARCE when any government-facing artifact exists, even a thin one. Reserve INFORMATION-ABSENT for companies with truly zero footprint across all search dimensions.
STEALTH-COMPANY PROTOCOL: Some legitimate defense companies operate in deliberate operational security (opsec) stealth - no public website, no press coverage, no Crunchbase profile - because their technology is sensitive. This is distinct from pre-operational companies that have built nothing.
LEGITIMATE OPSEC STEALTH (evaluable despite no public presence): Shows a GOVERNMENT-FACING FOOTPRINT despite no public-facing presence: SAM.gov registration, SBIR.gov awards, USASpending obligations, USPTO filings, clearance/FCL signals in any discoverable bio or reference. The government-facing footprint is sufficient to classify the company as INFORMATION-SCARCE on the affected criteria and apply the Classified-Program SCARCE Protocol.
PRE-OPERATIONAL WITH NOTHING: No footprint on EITHER the public-facing side OR the government-facing side - no SAM.gov registration, no SBIR.gov awards, no USASpending obligations, no USPTO filings, no clearance signals, no government program mentions anywhere in public records.
TEAM DIMENSION NOTE: The founding team's backgrounds are typically assessable even for stealth companies (LinkedIn profiles, conference bios, alumni records). Do not default the team dimension (C1) to INFORMATION-SCARCE solely because the company is in stealth. C1 is assessed on the available team signals; apply INFORMATION-SCARCE only to team-specific dimensions that are genuinely undisclosed (e.g., number of FTEs when the company has no online presence).
OUTPUT FLAG (Block 1): Add the field [STEALTH-MODE - government-facing corroboration: PRESENT / ABSENT]. PRESENT: at least one government-facing artifact found; applies INFORMATION-SCARCE protocol with corroborating artifact cited. ABSENT: no government-facing footprint; affected criteria score INFORMATION-ABSENT (lowest band) rather than INFORMATION-SCARCE.

Any deviation from the client's original specifications in the scoring criteria, weights, or band definitions must be documented in a Market Context Note at the point of deviation. The evaluator has latitude to adjust, reorder, replace, or add criteria relative to the original specifications, provided deviations are disclosed. Defense-specific Market Context Note required format strings - the hardware-vs-software track tag (HW/SW), the dual-use focus-risk indicator, the stale-tier indicator, and the CFIUS sub-threshold notation - are defined in Section 5 Block 1.

Both profiles score on a base scale of 100 points. The Sector Market-Event Modifier on the Sector criterion (A2/B2) can adjust the total by up to plus or minus 2 points, producing an operative scoring range of 98-102 points. Fundability tier thresholds are defined in absolute point values and apply across the full scoring range. The C2 Sector Market-Event Modifier is the sole envelope-expanding mechanism.
DESIGN CONSTRAINT: This instrument uses an additive, independent-criterion scoring architecture. No criterion modifies another criterion's score; the C2 sector modifier is the only mechanism that moves the total off 100. When a single development (such as a CFIUS inquiry, a program cancellation, or a key-person departure) affects multiple criteria simultaneously, the independent scoring structure cannot express the correlated risk quantitatively. Evaluators should describe cross-criterion risk correlations qualitatively in the Top 3 Fundability Risks (Block 5) and Fundraising Outlook (Block 5) sections of the output. The quantitative scores for each criterion remain independently assessed per their respective band definitions.
CROSS-CRITERION SYMMETRY: When a single risk affects multiple criteria and appears in multiple Top 3 Fundability Risk entries in Block 5, each risk entry must note the correlation to the other affected criteria. A cross-criterion risk described from only one direction understates its aggregate impact on the evaluation.
OPERATIONAL VIABILITY CONDITION ANCHORS: The OVC anchors are C1 (Team) AND C3 (Traction). When the company scores in its lowest defined band on BOTH C1 and C3, C2 (Sector) is capped at the lower-mid ceiling AND the Sector Market-Event Modifier's positive range is suppressed (modifier maximum 0): no positive modifier may apply, while an earned, named-and-dated NEGATIVE modifier still applies in full. The suppression binds POSITIVE modifiers only - it exists to stop sector-driven inflation and never cancels a documented negative event. This is the "Fool's Gold" guard: a hot Tier-1 sector score cannot inflate a company that has neither a credible team nor any traction. Full mechanism in A2/B2.

section.name: Routing Logic
section.block:
Every company evaluated under this instrument must first be routed to Profile A or Profile B. Routing is based on three required inputs: (1) the company's target raise size; (2) the company's development stage selected from the DDST enumerated taxonomy below; and (3) the company's investor composition characterized by the four-tier classification in Section 5 Block 1. The routing decision is made before any criterion is scored. A routing rationale that fails to ADDRESS one of the three inputs is a format error; recording a degraded confidence state for an input (below) ADDRESSES it - a missing or degraded raise figure is an evidence state to be dispositioned under the rules of this block, not a compliance failure.
RAISE-INPUT CONFIDENCE STATE (required): the target-raise input carries one of three confidence states, recorded in Block 1 - CONFIRMED (a stated figure from the company or a primary source), LOW-CONFIDENCE (a figure exists but is provisional, dated, or secondhand), or ABSENT (no figure in any source). LOW-CONFIDENCE and ABSENT are the routing-layer analogs of Section 1.5's INFORMATION-SCARCE and INFORMATION-ABSENT classifications.
TRIANGULATION UNDER A DEGRADED RAISE INPUT: when the raise input is ABSENT or LOW-CONFIDENCE, the evaluator is authorized to route on the secondary inputs (DDST stage plus investor composition) in ANY raise range - the authorization is not limited to the $2.5M-$3.5M gap band. The routing confidence must be recorded in the Block-1 Routing Rationale, and the re-route risk (a later-confirmed raise figure re-routing the company to the other profile) must be surfaced as a fundability risk in Block 5. Raise absence ALONE does not block scoring where triangulation is available.
INPUT-PRIORITY RULE (conflicts): for profile selection, the fundraising-ENVIRONMENT inputs (raise size and investor composition) outrank DDST product maturity. When the DDST stage points to one profile and both environment inputs point to the other, route on the environment inputs and document the conflict in the Routing Rationale: the instrument evaluates fundraising velocity, and the profile is the raise environment, not the engineering stage.
ROUTING-DEFERRED - CONFIRMATION REQUIRED (terminal disposition; same determination-state family as the Section 2.3 contingent gate disposition): when the raise input is ABSENT AND the secondary inputs cannot support a confident triangulation (e.g., investor composition also unassessable), routing is deferred pending input confirmation - record ROUTING-DEFERRED - CONFIRMATION REQUIRED in Block 1, state the input that would resolve it, and do not score. Where the deferral coincides with an enumerated Section 2.2 scope state (e.g., Out of Scope - No US Defense Nexus), the scope state governs and is recorded per Section 2.2.
DEFENSE DEVELOPMENT STAGE TAXONOMY (DDST) - eight ordered stages DS-0 through DS-7, sharing one spine across software-primary and hardware-intensive companies, forking only at DS-5 and re-converging at DS-6/DS-7. This taxonomy serves the dual function FDA regulatory stage serves in LS v5.1: it anchors routing logic AND product-maturity signal context.
DS-0: Concept / Pre-Prototype - IP, research, or concept only; nothing demonstrated in hardware or software. Observable: patent filings or published research; founding thesis; no SAM.gov/SBIR.gov record (or a pending application only).
DS-1: Working Prototype (Undemonstrated) - A functional prototype or alpha software exists but has not been shown in an operational or exercise context. Observable: demo videos, technical whitepapers, lab/bench test data; company product page; possibly a pending Phase I.
DS-2: SBIR/STTR Phase I (Feasibility Validated) - A government entity has competitively funded a feasibility study. Observable: SBIR.gov Phase I award record; AFWERX/NavalX/Army-AAL SBIR listing.
DS-3: Operational / Exercise Demonstration - Technology demonstrated in a controlled military exercise, wargame, or government-witnessed test. Observable: DoD/service press referencing exercise participation (Project Convergence, RIMPAC, Northern Edge, EDGE, similar); DIU/AFWERX demo announcements.
DS-4: Funded Prototype (Phase II or DIU/AFWERX/NavalX OTA prototype) - Competitively selected, substantial government R&D funding for prototype development. Co-equal entries: SBIR Phase II and a DIU OT prototype award are both DS-4 entries; the DIU OT is modestly stronger as a fielding/transition vehicle. Observable: SBIR.gov Phase II record; DIU/AFWERX OT award on USASpending.gov or press.
DS-5: Production-Eligible Transition. FORKS BY TRACK: Software/cyber sub-track: DS-5(SW) = ATO/cATO granted, IL4-IL6 authorization, or FedRAMP authorization. Observable: ATO announcement in press or company site; FedRAMP Marketplace listing; IL authorization announcement. Hardware sub-track: DS-5(HW) = SBIR Phase III, prototype-OT to production-OT conversion (section 4022(f)), qualification/type-classification, or Blue UAS listing. Observable: SBIR.gov Phase III record; production-OT announcement on USASpending or press; Blue UAS list; qualification/type-classification disclosure. A parallel manufacturing-throughput axis (units/month capacity) intensifies from DS-5(HW) onward.
DS-6: Contracted Revenue (Active Production/Service) - Revenue is flowing from active government or strategic contracts, possibly across multiple customers. Observable: announced contract values; multiple agency customers; revenue disclosed in funding PR; USASpending.gov obligations beyond R&D.
DS-7: Program of Record (Durable FYDP Demand) - A funded program line in the Future Years Defense Program. The apex pre-scaling demand signal (fewer than 1% of SBIR Phase I awardees reach it). Observable: budget documents (P-forms, R-forms); program-office PoR announcement; trade-press confirmation (Breaking Defense, DefenseScoop, Defense News).
Assign to Profile A if the company's target raise is $3M-$15M inclusive. Profile A companies are typically at DDST DS-5 through DS-7 with institutional Series A lead engagement and formal board governance. Profile A expects contracts, bookings, ATO/PoR trajectory, experienced operating teams with defense halo-employer or government-domain pedigree, and institutional-quality CFIUS-clean cap tables.
Assign to Profile B if the company's target raise is $500K to under $3M. Profile B companies are typically at DDST DS-0 through DS-4 with a seed-stage specialist lead, operator-angel syndicate, or accelerator-anchored composition. Profile B expects strong team and founder-market-fit signals, emerging government demand (Phase I, exercise demonstration, early award), and a clean SAFE-based or priced-seed cap table.
Companies targeting $2.5M-$3.5M fall in the gap between profiles. Resolve routing using the secondary inputs: route to Profile A if DDST is DS-5 or higher OR investor composition reflects a priced round led by a Defense-Specialist Institutional Lead; route to Profile B if DDST is DS-4 or lower AND investor composition is seed-stage (specialist seed lead, operator-angel syndicate, or non-dilutive-only). If still ambiguous, conduct a split evaluation under both profiles and report the score range, mirroring the LS/Tech gap protocol.
Companies with target raise below $500K but with at least one institutional participant are routed to Profile B with an INFORMATION-SCARCE flag. Companies with total raised under $275K and no institutional participation are classified Out of Scope - Pre-Seed Exclusion per Section 2.2.

The instrument is calibrated for private capital markets. Publicly traded companies, pre-seed companies (total raised under $275K with no institutional participation), post-close / not-currently-raising companies, and subjects with no US defense nexus are OUT OF SCOPE per the boundaries below. An OUT OF SCOPE flag is a scope/instrument mismatch, not a disqualifying deficiency. Out-of-scope companies may be evaluated as benchmark exercises if clearly flagged.
Companies whose target raise is $15M or below are IN SCOPE. Companies whose target raise exceeds $15M but is at or below $16.5M (10% above the $15M ceiling) are classified as GRAY ZONE. Gray Zone companies are evaluated under Profile A with a mandatory Gray Zone scope flag in the output. The evaluator must note the overshoot in the Routing Rationale and acknowledge that the instrument's calibration may be less precise for raises above $15M. Companies whose target raise exceeds $16.5M are OUT OF SCOPE and may only be evaluated as benchmark exercises with an Out of Scope - Benchmark flag.
Companies with target raise of $500K or above are IN SCOPE under Profile B. Companies with target raise below $500K but with at least one institutional participant (named VC fund or Tier 1/2 accelerator) are IN SCOPE with an INFORMATION-SCARCE flag, routed to Profile B. Companies with total raised under $275K AND no institutional participation are classified OUT OF SCOPE - Pre-Seed Exclusion. Pre-Seed Exclusion evaluations may proceed as benchmark exercises with an Out of Scope - Benchmark flag.
Companies that have JUST CLOSED a round and are not currently raising are OUT OF SCOPE - POST-CLOSE: the instrument evaluates active raises, and a completed round is a velocity outcome, not an evaluable fundraising posture. Record the closed round as a positive velocity datum (size, oversubscription, lead) in the evaluation record; do NOT force the company through the raise-size ceiling test as an overage. BOUNDARY (drawn tightly): this state applies ONLY where the dossier establishes the round is CLOSED and no active raise exists. A company that IS raising - on however thin a dossier, or with a degraded raise input - is IN SCOPE and is dispositioned under Section 2.1's raise-confidence rules; difficulty of evaluation never qualifies for this exit.
Subjects with NO US-defense footprint - foreign-domicile or purely commercial subjects where no US-government-facing artifact exists and the DDST taxonomy is unmappable (every DDST stage from DS-2 upward anchors on a US-government artifact) - are OUT OF SCOPE - NO US DEFENSE NEXUS. The Section 1.3 "globally applicable" claim presumes a US-defense nexus; where none exists, the instrument's reference frame does not apply. A NON-COMPARABILITY DISCLAIMER is a REQUIRED field in the evaluation record for this state: scores or observations produced in a benchmark exercise on such a subject are not comparable to in-scope evaluations. BOUNDARY (drawn tightly): this state applies ONLY to zero-US-defense-footprint subjects; a US-nexus company with a thin or degraded dossier is IN SCOPE and is dispositioned under Section 2.1 - difficulty of evaluation never qualifies for this exit.
The instrument is calibrated for software-primary and dual-use technology companies. Hardware-intensive companies - including pure hardware, autonomous systems with hardware dependence, defense kinetics, hypersonics, directed energy, space hardware, and maritime platforms - are within the general scope but produce persistent band language friction, most notably on C3 (where certification milestones and government contract revenue replace ARR), C6 (where higher burn tolerance and capex/grants substitute for lean-burn metrics), and C7-Moat (where manufacturing throughput and ITAR-protected know-how replace network effects). Application notes embedded within C3, C4, C6, and C7 provide an analog framework for hardware-intensive evaluations. This is a documented boundary condition, not a rubric deficiency. Evaluators must document the hardware classification in the Block 1 Market Context Note field, identify which criteria required analog application, and note that rubric fit limitations apply. Clients whose pipeline exceeds approximately 20% hardware-intensive companies should commission a dedicated hardware track (see Future Revisions Log FV-defense-1).
Target raise falls within the $500K-$15M range. Standard evaluation applies. Target raise exceeds $15M but is at or below $16.5M (10% tolerance). Evaluation proceeds under Profile A with a mandatory acknowledgment that instrument calibration may be less precise. Target raise exceeds $16.5M, or company is publicly traded. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged. Scores should not be compared directly to in-scope evaluations. Total raised under $275K with no institutional participation. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged. Round just closed; no active raise. Recorded as a velocity datum, not forced through the raise-size ceiling as an overage. Scope/instrument mismatch, not a disqualifying deficiency. No US-defense footprint; DDST unmappable. Non-comparability disclaimer REQUIRED in the evaluation record. Scope/instrument mismatch, not a disqualifying deficiency.

block.name: Automatic Disqualifiers
block.status: Defense ICP v1.0 - fourteen disqualifiers in five categories

section.block:
The defense instrument carries FOURTEEN automatic disqualifiers in FIVE categories: six defense-specific (Categories A and B) plus eight carried/adapted from the Tech ICP (Categories C, D, E). Two categories are NEW relative to both predecessors: (A) National Security and Export Control, and (B) Government Contracting Integrity. The two-level SBIR treatment (B2) is the key disqualifier-design decision: an adjudicated SBIR/FCA finding is a Block-2 gate; a behavioral SBIR-mill pattern is a scored deduction within C3 (Design Section 12B). Conditional disqualifiers (A3 FCL revocation; bid protest; full-time core leadership) default to a deduction/flag and gate only when core revenue is provably blocked/threatened. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE for the mill-vs-adjudicated boundary thresholds and the founder-ownership thresholds carried from Tech ICP.
The following conditions trigger automatic disqualification regardless of score. A disqualified company is classified as Out of Scope and does not receive a fundability tier assignment. If any disqualifier is triggered, the evaluation terminates after the Disqualifier Screen (Block 2 of the output format). No criterion scores, total score, or fundability tier are assigned. A score below 40 with no disqualifier triggered is classified as Tier 4 - Not Ready, not as Out of Scope. Out of Scope status is reserved for instrument scope mismatches and disqualifier triggers.
The disqualifiers are organized in five categories below: (A) National Security and Export Control; (B) Government Contracting Integrity; (C) Legal and IP; (D) Team Integrity; (E) Cap Table and Deal Structure. Mark each as CLEAR, TRIGGERED with explanation, NOT APPLICABLE where the non-applicability rule applies, or CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED where a gate's contingent disposition applies (defined for C1 and E1 below). Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification. Marking CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED does not trigger disqualification: the evaluation PROCEEDS, the open item is recorded as a Block-5 flag, and the named attestation is a mandatory pre-engagement condition. DETERMINATION-STATE COMPLETENESS RULE (construction convention, v2.0 and later): every gate, routing point, and classification point in this instrument must enumerate a disposition for the unverified/ambiguous evidence state, cross-referencing Section 1.5's INFORMATION-SCARCE / INFORMATION-ABSENT / ambiguous-defaults-to-SCARCE vocabulary; the evidence-tiered trigger grammar of D1/D2 and the conditional_escalation_rules is the house template, and a binary CLEAR/TRIGGERED authoring of a determination point is a construction error.
In addition to the automatic disqualifiers below, a scored_deductions element lists conditions that produce scored deductions within specific criteria rather than disqualification.
Foreign ownership, control, or influence that clearly blocks contract eligibility, with NO disclosed mitigation agreement (e.g., adversarial-state or PRC-linked investor with board or control rights; foreign co-founder controlling the entity without a mitigation agreement; a US investing fund with disqualifying foreign-LP control creating FOCI). Cap table and press (Crunchbase, PitchBook, Business Wire); sovereign/PRC-linked fund names; CFIUS-review news; NSIC/DFARS disclosures; SAM.gov entity registration; FOCI determination from DCSA when public. NOT a disqualifier where a DISCLOSED CFIUS MITIGATION AGREEMENT exists (scored as high-concern in C5 per Design Section 9A); or where foreign capital is allied-nation and non-controlling (moderate concern in C5). YES - sub-disqualifier CFIUS concern levels are scored in C5 (Design Section 9A band ceilings). Only unmitigated, eligibility-blocking FOCI triggers this gate.
A FINALIZED/ADJUDICATED export-control enforcement action against the company or its principals (civil penalty, consent agreement, or criminal conviction - the Vescent Photonics $400K-plus settlement for improper foreign-subcontractor use is the archetype). DDTC debarment list; BIS denial order list; DoJ press releases. An ITAR/EAR registration gap or open inquiry without adjudication is NOT this gate (C4 flag in the lowest band). Applies only to finalized enforcement. NO - adjudicated enforcement is binary.
An FCL revoked or suspended AND the company's CORE REVENUE requires the now-blocked classified work. Both conditions must be present. DCSA communications (sometimes public); company press; trade press. NOT a disqualifier where the company's core revenue does NOT depend on classified work (an FCL issue becomes a C4 deduction within the lower-mid band plus Block-5 flag). The conditionality is essential: many defense companies can continue commercially if their FCL is a supplementary capability. YES - non-core FCL issues are a C4 band deduction.
The company OR its principals appear as excluded parties in the SAM.gov exclusions database (debarred or suspended from federal contracting). SAM.gov exclusions list (public, searchable by company name or DUNS/UEI). NONE - active debarment is dispositive. NO.
An ADJUDICATED civil or criminal SBIR or False Claims Act finding against the company or founders. Archetype cases: TrellisWare Technologies (majority-owned subsidiary of ViaSat) - $12,177,631.90 settlement, SBIR ineligibility, DOJ/SDCA, March 12, 2018; Lithium Power Technologies - approximately $5M plus debarment; ML Energia - president convicted; Fractal Systems / Smart Polymers (Aldissi) - approximately $10.5M fraud, 15-year sentence. DoJ/OIG press releases; SBIR.gov fraud page; PACER court records. NONE for an adjudicated finding. YES - CRITICAL TWO-LEVEL TREATMENT. A BEHAVIORAL SBIR-MILL PATTERN (no adjudication) is a SCORED DEDUCTION within C3 (see Design Section 12B). The two levels: adjudicated finding = this Block-2 gate; behavioral pattern (many Phase I awards across agencies with no Phase II/III transition and no contract/commercial revenue, topic-hopping, or multi-year stall) = C3 scored deduction. This distinction is dispositive: this gate fires ONLY on an adjudicated finding.
A CRADA or government agreement whose specific terms BAR COMMERCIALIZATION or BLOCK INVESTOR RIGHTS such that venture returns are structurally impossible (not merely constrained). Disclosed agreements; press release terms; diligence. Gate applies only when the barring term is DOCUMENTED; possible terms that cannot be confirmed are Block-5 risk flags, not gates. Ordinary CRADAs and standard government-purpose data-rights provisions that do NOT bar commercialization are normal in defense and not a gate. YES - exclusivity that constrains (but does not bar) leads to a C5 independence deduction plus a Block-5 CVC independence flag.
CONFIRMED-ADVERSE EVIDENCE OR REFUSAL is required to trigger this gate. TRIGGERED when (i) CONFIRMED evidence establishes that the company's CORE (venture-thesis) IP is not assigned to the company - a confirmed assignment of core IP to a prior employer, a university or DARPA program, or a government program; a confirmed SBIR/STTR data-rights defect; or a confirmed TTO exclusive-license defect where the TTO retains rights that impair commercialization - OR (ii) the company refuses to confirm: Refusal to confirm IP assignment when directly asked is itself a triggering condition (refusal is an act, not an absence of records). CORE/NON-CORE QUALIFIER: the gate applies to the company's core venture-thesis IP, determined against the company's own stated thesis. A government- or prime-owned NON-CORE asset accessed via CRADA or license is NOT this gate - it routes to a Block-5 commercialization-structure flag. REVERSAL CONDITION: if the government- or prime-owned asset IS the core venture thesis, the gate TRIGGERS; the core/non-core determination and its basis must be documented in the Block-2 field. CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED (the third determination state, per Section 1.5's INFORMATION-SCARCE / INFORMATION-ABSENT / ambiguous-defaults-to-SCARCE vocabulary): when IP assignment is UNVERIFIED on available records (e.g., an unrecorded founder-inventor assignment, or pre-grant software IP with no USPTO trace) AND no refusal has occurred, the gate does NOT trigger. Mark CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED: the evaluation PROCEEDS; affected dimensions score per Section 1.5 (SCARCE/ABSENT discipline unchanged - this disposition licenses no midpoint default by itself); a Block-5 flag records the open item; and IP-assignment attestation is a MANDATORY PRE-ENGAGEMENT CONDITION. Absence of public assignment records is an evidence state, not a triggering condition. USPTO assignment records (public); TTO license terms; SBIR data-rights terms (often disclosed in SBIR awards); standard VC diligence question. NONE for a CONFIRMED core-IP assignment defect - confirmed unassigned core IP is dispositive for venture fundability. Minor, curable license gaps with a documented remediation path may be Block-5 flagged rather than gated, but only when the gap is genuinely minor and a remediation timeline is disclosed. (An unverified assignment posture with no refusal is not a gap in this sense; it takes the CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED disposition above.) NO (binary assignment defect); minor curable gaps lead to a Block-5 flag only.
A bid protest, False Claims Act action, or IP dispute that materially THREATENS THE COMPANY'S CORE REVENUE (not peripheral litigation). Both the existence of the litigation AND its core-revenue threat must be present. GAO bid-protest docket (public); PACER court records; press. Litigation that does NOT threaten core revenue (a typical bid protest by a competitor on a non-core award) leads to a Block-5 risk flag, not a gate. YES - non-core litigation leads to a Block-5 flag.
Active or past SECURITIES FRAUD history (SEC enforcement); OR WHOLESALE FALSIFICATION OF MILITARY SERVICE OR RANK - stolen-valor-grade fabrication (not minor exaggeration, which is handled by the NCSP deduction in C1). SEC litigation releases; court records (PACER); Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) military records when public. NONE for fabrication. Minor service-claim exaggeration is the NCSP deduction in C1 (Design Section 5D), not this gate. YES - minor exaggeration leads to a C1 NCSP deduction per Design Section 5D. Wholesale fabrication triggers the gate.
Wholesale fabrication of educational credentials, professional role history, or institutional affiliation - not mere embellishment or title inflation (which is the NCSP minor-contradiction deduction). Public records; institutional verification; LinkedIn cross-check against company filings. NONE for wholesale fabrication. YES - embellishment short of fabrication leads to a C1 NCSP minor-contradiction deduction.
The CORE CEO or CTO is part-time or uncommitted with NO DOCUMENTED FULL-TIME TRANSITION PLAN. Applies only to CEO and CTO roles, not to other team members. LinkedIn current-employer field; company disclosures; concurrent-role signals. NOT APPLICABLE where a documented full-time transition timeline is published or attested. ALSO NOT APPLICABLE to part-time senior advisors or fractional non-core roles - these are NORMAL in defense (common among senior military/IC alumni) and do not trigger this gate. Only the core CEO/CTO part-time status (without a transition plan) is dispositive. YES - the advisor-heavy / engineering-light pattern is a C1 NCSP deduction (Design Section 5D, "advisor-heavy team inflation" contradiction type), not this gate.
CONFIRMED-ADVERSE EVIDENCE OR REFUSAL is required to trigger this gate. TRIGGERED when (i) CONFIRMED evidence establishes a sporadic, messy, or structurally compromised cap table - confirmed unresolved ownership disputes, confirmed dead equity, confirmed material terms that were undisclosed and have surfaced adverse, or confirmed legal encumbrances - OR (ii) the company refuses: Refusal to provide a cap table summary by band when directly asked is itself a triggering condition (refusal is an act, not an absence of records). RE-ROUTED STATE ITEMS: bare "missing documentation" and bare "undisclosed material terms" - the default condition of a pre-diligence seed dossier - are evidence states, not triggers; they take the CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED disposition below unless and until disclosure or diligence CONFIRMS a defect, at which point the gate triggers on the confirmed evidence. CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED (the third determination state, per Section 1.5's INFORMATION-SCARCE / INFORMATION-ABSENT / ambiguous-defaults-to-SCARCE vocabulary): an undisclosed cap table with NO refusal on direct request does NOT trigger this gate. Mark CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED: the evaluation PROCEEDS; C5 scores per Section 1.5 and its own band definitions; a Block-5 flag records the open item; and a cap-table summary by band (founder attestation by band acceptable) is a MANDATORY PRE-ENGAGEMENT CONDITION. Non-disclosure is an evidence state; refusal is the act that triggers. Cap-table diligence; founder attestation by band; prior-round filings; pattern of refusal across multiple direct questions. NONE. NO.
Aggregate founder/CEO ownership below approximately 10% post-Seed or below 15% post-Series A, without explanation (e.g., recapitalization, prior exit). Cap-table diligence; founder attestation by band; LTSE/Carta benchmark comparison. NONE. NO. [TENTATIVE - thresholds carried verbatim from Tech ICP; re-confirm against the defense cohort where heavy non-dilutive funding may alter typical ownership trajectories.]
Stacked SAFEs exceeding $3M total with no priced round in 24-plus months. Funding-history records; founder attestation; Crunchbase round history; explicit absence of a priced round in the funding timeline. NONE. SAFE stacks below $3M, or any SAFE stack with a priced round within 24 months, are handled as scored deductions within C5, not as disqualifiers. NO (for the $3M-plus-no-priced-round combination); sub-threshold SAFE stacks are a C5 within-band deduction.
The following conditions are NOT automatic disqualifiers but produce scored deductions within their respective criteria (or Block-5 flags). They are listed here for evaluator routing reference; documentation occurs at the criterion level.
CFIUS sub-threshold concern (high-concern, mitigated, or allied/opaque): C5 band caps per Design Section 9A (high-concern leads to lower-mid cap; moderate/opaque leads to upper-mid cap). SBIR mill behavioral pattern (no adjudication): C3 scored deduction per Design Section 12B (moderate signature reduces C3 by approximately 25-40% of its points or drops one band; severe signature drops to C3 lowest band). CVC exclusivity/independence constraint (constrains but does not bar): C5 independence deduction plus Block-5 CVC independence flag. CMMC absence where the contract type requires it: C4 within-band deduction (not a disqualifier). Minor NCSP contradictions (title inflation, minor service-claim exaggeration, embellishment short of fabrication): C1 deductions per Design Section 5D. Single-program / single-customer dependency: C7-Exit sub-component cap at the lower-mid ceiling (Design Section 10C). Non-core FCL revocation/suspension: C4 within-band deduction plus Block-5 flag (escalates to disqualifier A3 only if core revenue requires the blocked classified work). Active bid protest naming the company that does NOT threaten core revenue: Block-5 risk flag (escalates to disqualifier C2 only if it threatens core revenue). ITAR/EAR registration absence where the product plainly requires it (no adjudication): C4 flag in the lowest band (escalates to disqualifier A2 only on adjudicated enforcement).
CONDITIONAL ESCALATION RULES (PCDB Design Section 11 Decision 7): (1) Active bid protest naming the company defaults to a Block-5 risk flag; escalates to the C2 disqualifier only if it threatens core revenue - a protest is common and frequently resolved. (2) Facility-Clearance revoked/suspended defaults to a C4 Access deduction plus Block-5 flag; escalates to the A3 conditional disqualifier only when core revenue requires the blocked classified work. (3) Lack of full-time core-leadership commitment applies only to the core CEO/CTO without a transition plan; part-time senior advisors are normal in defense and do not trigger D3.

criterion.name: Team Quality and Defense-Domain Credibility
criterion.revision_note: Three-family defense halo-employer taxonomy (Design Section 5A) replaces the Tech ICP commercial halo set and the LS KOL framework. Founder-Market Fit is a scored sub-component positioned within the team band (the Tech ICP convention). Solo-founder protocol carried from Tech ICP with a defense exception (Design Section 5C). NCSP transfers from Tech/LS with defense-specific contradiction types (Design Section 5D); stolen-valor-grade falsified service escalates to the Block-2 disqualifier D1. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the defense-specific NCSP contradiction types and the operator-vs-engineer pedigree balance have not been empirically calibrated.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the founding/executive team's demonstrated ability to build and field defense technology and to transact with the government. Measures a blend of (i) technical/engineering pedigree and (ii) operational/government-domain credibility (founder-market fit). Dominant fundraising-velocity predictor at both profiles (research Workstream 2b). Bands are near stage-invariant; the Profile-A delta is noted. Single most heavily weighted criterion.
criterion.band: At least one founder/key executive from a Tier-1 defense halo employer (see halo_employer_taxonomy) in a role demonstrating real technical depth or program authority - OR a complementary pair: a Tier-1 technical founder PLUS a Tier-1 operational/acquisition founder (the engineer-CEO plus operator pattern). Two or more Founder-Market-Fit signals present (e.g., prior end-user deployment in the exact domain AND government-side acquisition/program experience). Demonstrated development capacity (named engineering leads / shipped prototype), not advisor-fronted; the team can build, not merely convene. Clearance-eligible or cleared key personnel where the domain requires it. A-DELTA: at Profile A, evidence the team has EXECUTED a government contract or fielded a system (a prior exit or an executed government contract under this team), not merely won an award, can anchor the top band.

Credible technical pedigree from Tier-2 sources plus some domain credibility, but missing EITHER elite technical depth OR deep operational/acquisition experience; OR strong Tier-2 coverage across both dimensions. One FMF signal present; founder-market fit is plausible but not richly corroborated. Development capacity demonstrated but thin (small technical bench).

Relevant background but thin on BOTH the technical-depth and operational-domain dimensions (e.g., a strong commercial-tech team new to defense with limited domain credibility; or operators with development capacity still being built). FMF asserted via domain employment/education but no public artifacts (INFORMATION-SCARCE leads to midpoint within this band). No cleared personnel where the domain will require clearances.

No relevant defense-domain or elite-technical pedigree. "Advisor-heavy / engineering-light" - many senior advisors/retired flag officers on the masthead, near-zero technical FTEs (the War College "Fool's Gold" pattern); triggers NCSP review (Design Section 5D). Founder identity/background uncorroborated by third-party sources (INFORMATION-ABSENT, not SCARCE).
criterion.halo_employer_taxonomy:
DEFENSE HALO-EMPLOYER TAXONOMY (three credibility families, each with Tier-1 and Tier-2 designations; exemplary, not exhaustive - "or equivalent" framing applies). [Tier-1/Tier-2 company assignments are a 2025-2026 snapshot and will drift; re-confirm at tier-table re-versioning per Design Section 12D.]
Family (i) - Pure-defense companies (alumni networks): Tier 1: Anduril, Palantir, SpaceX, Shield AI (the recurring "Palantir/PayPal/SpaceX mafia" pattern; founder lineage from these firms is the strongest commercial-defense pedigree signal). Tier 2: Saronic, Castelion, Vannevar, Epirus, Rebellion Defense, Skydio and comparable scaled venture-backed defense companies; primes' elite advanced units (Lockheed Skunk Works, Northrop advanced programs).
Family (ii) - Government / IC / military programs: Tier 1: DARPA program managers; DIU fellows/leadership; In-Q-Tel investment/technical staff; IC officers in relevant programs; special-operations (SOF) officers in a domain relevant to the company's product; senior PEO/acquisition leaders. Tier 2: broader military service (non-SOF, relevant branch/MOS); program-office staff below PM; service-lab technical staff.
Family (iii) - Academic / research institutions: Tier 1: MIT Lincoln Laboratory, JHU Applied Physics Laboratory (APL), MITRE, SRI, other FFRDCs/UARCs, and DARPA-funded principal investigators. Tier 2: high-pedigree commercial deep-tech research backgrounds (Tesla, NVIDIA, Google AI/DeepMind) paired with a defense-domain co-founder; strong university research programs without a defense nexus on their own.
Band logic uses the taxonomy directly: TOP requires Tier-1 pedigree in EITHER the technical or the operational/government family AND complementary depth in the other dimension; UPPER-MID requires Tier-1 in one dimension with thinner coverage in the other OR strong Tier-2 across both; LOWER-MID is relevant background thin on both dimensions; LOWEST is no relevant pedigree or the advisor-fronted Fool's-Gold pattern.
criterion.scored_sub_component:
Founder-Market Fit is scored within the A1 band assignment as a sub-component rather than a standalone criterion (the Tech ICP NRR/FMF convention - it outputs a position within the band, never a number, and cannot change the band). Defense FMF "earned-secret" signals, ordered: - Prior DEPLOYMENT in a relevant operational context. - Prior ACQUISITION/PROCUREMENT experience from the government side. - Prior CLASSIFIED-PROGRAM experience (existence observable via clearance/bio signals even where details are INFORMATION-SCARCE). - Prior experience as an END-USER of the class of system the company builds. - PUBLISHED WRITING / CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS on the operational problem (the defense analog of the Rachleff/Maples/Sequoia Arc "earned secret" test).
SCORING RULE: two or more corroborated FMF signals position the team at the TOP of its current band; one signal positions at the middle; none positions at the lower portion of the band. FMF never moves the team across bands by itself. The Justification field must explicitly state the FMF signal assessment. All "classified-program experience" handling uses the INFORMATION-SCARCE track (midpoint within band, justified, with a named corroborating artifact) - never penalize undisclosed-but-corroborated clearance/program signals (Design Section 12A).
criterion.solo_founder_protocol:
SOLO-FOUNDER TREATMENT (carried from Tech ICP with a defense exception): apply a 2-3 point deduction at Profile A for a solo founder, with permission to drop to the next lower band if the deduction would exceed the band floor (mirroring NCSP material-contradiction mechanics). The greater Profile A penalty (vs. Profile B's 1-point deduction) reflects that institutional Series A leads are systematically less accepting of solo founders.
DEFENSE EXCEPTIONS (either suffices to waive the deduction): (1) the solo founder is a Tier-1 individual (e.g., former DARPA PM, senior PEO, senior SOF/IC leader) AND has assembled a NAMED, CREDIBLE TECHNICAL BENCH (so the company is not "general-on-the-payroll" with no development capacity); OR (2) the founder has a prior exit above $500M (the inherited Tech ICP exception).
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: When the solo-founder deduction is applied or waived, the A1 Justification field must explicitly state the deduction magnitude (or the waiving exception) and the resulting score position within the band.
criterion.negative_credibility_protocol:
NEGATIVE CREDIBILITY SIGNAL PROTOCOL (defense contradiction types): Before finalizing the A1 score, the evaluator must assess whether any credibility claims made by the team are directly contradicted by verifiable evidence. Verifiable evidence includes: title records (LinkedIn, company website, filings); SBIR.gov award PI records; public military records / Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC); Blue UAS list membership and SBIR Phase II awardee records; competitor existence data.
Defense-specific contradiction types: - Misrepresented military service or rank (cross-check LinkedIn/bio against public military records / DMDC). STOLEN-VALOR-GRADE fabrication escalates beyond a deduction to the Team-Integrity disqualifier D1 (Design Section 11); minor exaggeration is the deduction below. - Claimed security clearances that cannot be verified (clearance existence is sometimes verifiable; level usually not). - Exaggerated government program participation or advisory roles. - False SBIR authorship / PI attribution (cross-check SBIR.gov award PI records). - "Advisor-heavy / engineering-light" team inflation (many senior advisors/retired flag officers, near-zero technical FTEs). - Claimed "first-in-class" positioning contradicted by existing Blue UAS list members or SBIR Phase II awardees in the same sub-sector.
CLASSIFICATION RULE (deduction predicate): a deduction under this protocol requires NAMED CONTRADICTING EVIDENCE - a specific claim and the specific verifiable source that contradicts it. An UNVERIFIED-UNCORROBORATED claim (plausible but not confirmable - e.g., a structurally non-public clearance claim, or an in-window provisional patent with no public trace) is NOT a contradiction and never earns a credibility deduction; it is classified and routed to evidence-band placement per Section 1.5 (INFORMATION-SCARCE / INFORMATION-ABSENT) and, where diligence-material, recorded as a Block-5 flag. The "first-in-class" strict predicate is unchanged. If one or more contradictions are identified, apply a deduction within the assigned band as follows: MINOR CONTRADICTION(S): informal title inflation, modest overstatement, or comparable promotional items - each contradicted by a named source - where the AGGREGATE SEVERITY of the set remains minor. Apply a 1-point deduction within the assigned band; do not drop below the band floor. Multiple genuinely-minor promotional items REMAIN in this bucket unless their aggregate severity warrants escalation; the severity basis for keeping or escalating must be documented. MATERIAL CONTRADICTION (severity-keyed, not count-keyed): a single materially false claim, OR a cluster of contradicted claims whose AGGREGATE SEVERITY is material. Apply a 2-3 point deduction within the assigned band; the evaluator may drop to the next lower band if the deduction would exceed the band floor. The Justification must state the severity basis for the bucket assignment (why the item or cluster is material) - an item count alone never assigns this bucket. NO CONTRADICTIONS IDENTIFIED: No deduction. Score per band definitions on their merits.
This protocol applies regardless of whether the midpoint-default is in effect. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: The Justification field must name each contradiction, identify the source that contradicts it, state the deduction applied, and record the classification of any unverified items considered (classified as Section 1.5 evidence states under the Classification Rule, not as contradictions). When no contradictions are found, a one-sentence statement is sufficient: "Negative Credibility Signal Protocol applied - no contradicted claims identified."

criterion.name: Sector and Market Alignment
criterion.revision_note: Four-tier base classification (Tier 1 PEAK / Tier 2 ACTIVE / Tier 3 SELECTIVE / Out-of-Favor) from the dated defense sector tier table (research Workstream 3; PCDB DS-4). A SINGLE Sector Market-Event Modifier (plus/minus 2) replaces the Tech ICP's three-component modifier structure - it is not split into AI / M&A / dual-use components. Dual-use carries no modifier and no band adjustment; it is qualitative-only (Block 5). The OVC anchors are C1 (Team) and C3 (Traction). The tier-table staleness mechanism (Design Section 12D) caps the modifier at plus/minus 1 when the table is stale. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the M&A enterprise-value modifier bands and the appropriations +1/+2 boundary are anchored on few comps.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates whether the company operates in a defense sub-sector currently attracting investor capital and program demand. Two parts: a four-tier base classification (general appetite, from the dated tier table) and a single Sector Market-Event Modifier (plus/minus 2). Stage-invariant. Subject to the OVC cap (this criterion is the capped criterion, not an OVC anchor).
criterion.band: Sub-sector is on the current Tier 1 list: Autonomy/UAS; Counter-UAS; Defense AI / C4ISR / mission software; Space/ISR-from-space. Multiple rounds of $20M or more at Seed-A and active M&A/IPO motion in the sub-sector within the trailing 12 months. Appropriations trend rising; named program demand exists (e.g., Replicator/Drone Dominance, Golden Dome adjacency). TIER-1 ENGAGEMENT TEST: Tier-1 appetite credit requires DEMONSTRATED defense engagement - at least one government-facing artifact (SBIR.gov or USASpending record, SAM.gov registration with defense activity, a DIU/AFWERX/prime announcement, or documented exercise participation) - not a sub-sector string-match. A defense-claiming company with zero government-facing artifacts does not earn Tier-1 credit on naming alone; classify it per the sub-sector its DEMONSTRATED positioning supports, or per the default-tier rule if off-table after the table check. The engagement artifact must be cited in the Justification wherever Tier-1 credit is granted.

Sub-sector on the current Tier 2 list: Maritime autonomy; Hypersonics/directed energy; Cyber/zero-trust; Logistics/supply-chain; Defense electronics; EW/SIGINT. Funding present but thinner or expanding from a smaller base; some M&A.

Sub-sector on the current Tier 3 list: Quantum for defense; Biodefense/CBRN; Human performance/soldier systems; Training and simulation; Enabling/infrastructure segments (MBSE, digital-engineering, and defense "picks-and-shovels" tooling) [added v2.0 - assigned Tier 3: appetite is real but selective and thesis-driven; assignment stops these segments from landing on the default rule]. Niche or mixed-trajectory funding; selective, thesis-driven investor interest only.
Pure services / labor-intensive low-growth; single-program hardware with no commercial or transition path; SBIR-mill R&D shops; sub-sectors with documented contraction.
criterion.default_tier_rule: DEFAULT-TIER RULE: if the sub-sector is not on the dated tier table, default to Tier 3 / lower-mid and document the classification basis in the A2 Justification (mirrors the Tech ICP default-tier rule). PRECEDENCE: explicit band criteria govern over the default - a sub-sector meeting a documented band condition (e.g., the Out-of-Favor band's documented-contraction criterion) classifies by that band, never by the default. The default is an admission of ignorance about investor appetite, invoked ONLY after the tier table's named entries have been checked; the Justification must state the table row(s) checked before the default was invoked.
criterion.sector_tier_table_versioning:
SECTOR TIER TABLE VERSIONING: The sector tier classification above reflects the 2025-2026 snapshot (version date: v2026-Q2). Defense sub-sector investor appetite moves with Congressional appropriations and battlefield lessons faster than commercial sectors. The tier table must be re-evaluated: (i) at least annually; (ii) on each NDAA or full-year appropriations enactment; and (iii) on any mandatory trigger event - a new mega-program (Golden-Dome-scale appropriation), a marquee M&A (BlueHalo-scale enterprise value), a major program cancellation, a Replicator-scale procurement announcement, or a documented sector-wide multiple compression or shakeout.
STALENESS NOTATION: When the analysis date is MORE THAN 12 MONTHS after the tier-table version date (v2026-Q2), or when a mandatory trigger event has occurred since the version date, the evaluator must: (a) stamp Block 0 with [SECTOR TIER TABLE STALE - v2026-Q2]; (b) stamp Block 5 with the same flag; (c) CAP the Sector Market-Event Modifier at plus/minus 1 (not plus/minus 2) until the tier table is re-versioned. A stale tier table cannot drive a full plus/minus 2 swing.

component.name: Sector Market-Event Modifier
component.status: Defense ICP v1.0 - single modifier (NOT split into multiple components)
component.instruction: This is the SINGLE combined modifier on C2 - it is not split into two or three components. After assigning the base tier score, apply the modifier below. A modifier value other than 0 MUST cite a specific named event with a date in the C2 Justification; a non-zero modifier with no named event is a FORMAT ERROR. The modifier adjusts the base score and may cause the final C2 score to exceed the base tier ceiling or fall below the base tier floor (operative envelope 98-102). When the tier table is stale (see sector_tier_table_versioning), cap this modifier at plus/minus 1.
component.modifier: A tens-of-billions appropriations program that redefines the sub-sector (e.g., the $151B Golden Dome initiative for space/missile-defense adjacency); OR a strategic acquisition with enterprise value greater than $3B (e.g., BlueHalo / AeroVironment, approximately $4.1B); OR a flagship Program-of-Record designation that anchors the sub-sector (e.g., Palantir Maven Smart System); OR a large Replicator / Drone Dominance-scale procurement.

A marquee appropriations increase that lifts a SPECIFIC sub-sector without redefining the whole sector (e.g., the near-doubling of Army small-cUAS to approximately $994M in FY2027); OR a strategic acquisition in the $300M-$3B range (e.g., Leidos-Kudu Dynamics, $300M). NOTE: the $994M Army small-cUAS event is assigned +1, NOT +2 - it materially lifts counter-UAS specifically but does not redefine the defense sector as a whole.
No documented marquee event in the trailing window; ordinary deal flow only. The base tier score stands without adjustment.
A documented program cancellation or appropriations cut affecting the sub-sector; OR a marquee down-round or shutdown of a comparable company.
A sector-wide multiple compression or shakeout event (the Stephens scenario), or a sub-sector-defining cancellation that resets investor appetite.

criterion.operational_viability_condition:
OPERATIONAL VIABILITY CONDITION: Before finalizing the A2 score, apply the following gate (the "Fool's Gold" guard).
TRIGGER: If the company scores in its lowest defined band on BOTH A1 (Team Quality and Defense-Domain Credibility, Band 0-5) AND A3 (Product, Traction and Government Demand, Band 0-4 "Under-Traction for Stage"), the A2 final score (base tier score plus any Sector Market-Event Modifier) is capped at the lower-mid ceiling (A2 max 7) AND the Sector Market-Event Modifier's positive range is suppressed (modifier maximum 0): no positive modifier may apply; an earned, named-and-dated NEGATIVE modifier still applies in full (the suppression binds positive modifiers only).
RATIONALE: When the company has neither a credible team (lowest A1 band) nor any traction (lowest A3 band), a hot Tier-1 sector score cannot be monetized regardless of how favorable sector conditions are. The AND condition prevents penalizing companies with a strong team but absent traction (or vice versa). The anchors are C1 (Team) and C3 (Traction), directly implementing research Design-Risk #1.
CAP VALUE: A2 capped at 7 (the lower-mid band ceiling); modifier maximum 0 (positive range suppressed; a documented negative modifier still applies).
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: When triggered, document in the A2 Justification: (a) the A1 and A3 scores that triggered the cap; (b) the uncapped A2 score that would have applied; (c) the capped score recorded. When not triggered, a one-sentence confirmation is sufficient: "Operational Viability Condition not triggered - A1=[X] and/or A3=[X] above threshold."

criterion.name: Product, Traction and Government Demand
criterion.revision_note: Defined separately for Profile A (contract, bookings, and durability signals). There is no universal ARR analog; the pre-contract "ARR analog" is government bookings/contract backlog and non-dilutive award value, and the contract-stage signals are bookings, ATO/PoR trajectory, and multi-customer adoption. SBIR-Progression Quality is a scored sub-component with a mill-signature branch (Design Sections 6C / 12B). One of the two OVC anchors (with C1). EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the Profile-A dollar anchors derive from a single Breaking Defense benchmark and the Vannevar comp; the SBIR-mill numeric thresholds are analyst-set.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the maturity and credibility of the company's product and the strength of demonstrated government demand. At Series A, evidence of contracts, bookings, ATO/PoR trajectory, and multi-customer adoption dominates. Research benchmark anchors: approximately $10M contracts/bookings supports a ~$25M Series A; approximately $20M-plus booked annual revenue supports a $40-50M Series B; Vannevar reached ~$25M sales / 15 agencies before its $75M Series B.
criterion.scope_note: SCOPE NOTE - C3 vs. C4: Awards, contracts, and revenue derived from government programs are scored in C3 (Product, Traction and Government Demand). Security clearances, facility clearances, authorizations (ATO/IL/FedRAMP/CMMC), ITAR/EAR registration, procurement vehicle eligibility, and program-office relationships are scored exclusively in C4 (Government Access and Procurement Pathway). An ATO grant is scored in C4 as an access credential; its resulting contract revenue is scored in C3. No single artifact or relationship is scored in both criteria.
criterion.band: Substantial contracted backlog/bookings (approximately $10M or more supporting the raise) AND a durability signal: production-OT, SBIR Phase III, PoR trajectory, or (software) a granted ATO/cATO - and/or multiple agency customers. DS-6/DS-7 (contracted revenue at volume / PoR). A granted ATO contributes to this top band ONLY when paired with contract revenue (ATO plus bookings equals durability evidence); a Program-of-Record designation is a top-band signal in its own right.

Meaningful contracts/bookings (approximately $3M-$10M) with at least one transition/production-eligible signal (Phase III, production-OT, or ATO), but not yet multi-customer scale or a PoR. DS-5 reached. A single STRATFI/TACFI award sits in this upper-mid band (strong government plus matched private validation, not yet production revenue or a PoR).
Early awards (Phase II / DIU OT, DS-4) with bookings below approximately $3M and no production-eligible transition yet.

Only Phase I or a prototype at a Series A raise level (DS-1/DS-2) - a red flag of stage/traction mismatch. Marketing claims of "interest" with no SBIR.gov/USASpending corroboration (INFORMATION-ABSENT).
criterion.scored_sub_component:
SBIR-PROGRESSION QUALITY (scored as position-within-band inside C3; the mill signature additionally drives the Design Section 12B scored deduction). Baseline (healthy): approximately 40-60% of applying Phase I awardees convert to Phase II.
Positioning: - Strong progression (top of band): a clean Phase I to Phase II to Phase III / production-OT / PoR transition path, with transition to a real customer. - Healthy / in-progress (middle): Phase I to Phase II with a credible (not yet executed) transition plan. - Thin (lower portion): Phase I awards only, early, no Phase II yet (consistent with stage). - Mill signature (deduction): drops the within-band position to the floor and triggers the scored deduction below.
SBIR-MILL BEHAVIORAL DETECTION (scored deduction within C3, NOT a disqualifier; the adjudicated case is the Block-2 B2 gate). Mill-signature triggers (ANY ONE is sufficient) [all TENTATIVE]: - a Phase I to Phase II conversion rate below 20% across 5 or more Phase I awards; - 10 or more Phase I awards with 0 Phase III / 0 transition and 0 contract/commercial revenue; - 3 or more years with Phase I awards only and no transition and no contract/commercial revenue; - topic-hopping across unrelated agencies/topics with no through-line to a coherent product. Observability: SBIR.gov award records (counts, phases, dates, agencies, PI names); USASpending.gov transition/obligation records. Deduction magnitudes [TENTATIVE, aligned to NCSP magnitudes]: a MODERATE mill signature (one trigger) reduces the C3 score by approximately 25-40% of its maximum OR drops one band (analyst's choice, justified); a SEVERE mill signature (two or more triggers, or one trigger with extreme values) drops C3 to the lowest band. Connection to Block-2 gate: if an ADJUDICATED SBIR/FCA finding exists against the company or its founders (Block-2 gate B2), the C3 scoring is superseded - the evaluation terminates at Block 2. The C3 mill deduction applies ONLY to behavioral patterns without adjudication.
criterion.application_note: HARDWARE APPLICATION NOTE (counter-UAS kinetics, hypersonics, maritime hardware): ARR analogs do not apply; substitute contract backlog/bookings, units delivered/produced, demonstrated production rate (units/month), live-fire/qualification results, Blue UAS / type-classification status, and production-OT awards. A successful live-fire demo plus a production-OT plus demonstrated monthly capacity substitutes for "ARR" at the top band. Invoke when Block 1 Market Context Note tags the company hardware-intensive; cite in the C3 Justification.

SOFTWARE APPLICATION NOTE (defense-AI, C4ISR, cyber): substitute ATO/IL level, number of agency deployments/seats, recurring contract value, and integration onto a PoR platform (e.g., Maven Smart System, Lattice) for ARR. Invoke when Block 1 Market Context Note tags the company software-primary; cite in the C3 Justification.

criterion.name: Government Access and Procurement Pathway
criterion.status: Defense ICP v1.0 R4 - no predecessor analog
criterion.revision_note: A criterion with NO analog in either predecessor (LS folds regulatory status into FDA stage; Tech has no equivalent). Retained as standalone per Design Section 1 Decision 2. Stage-invariant: one profile delta only (authorizations scored as granted at Profile A vs. in-progress/credible-trajectory at Profile B). Procurement Pathway Literacy is a scored sub-component (Design Section 7D). EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the software-only ATO cap and the top-band sufficiency of relationships-alone are calibration items.
criterion.purpose: Government Access and Procurement Pathway measures the company's demonstrated capability to transact with the government - the clearances, authorizations, program-office relationships, and acquisition-pathway literacy required to convert demand into contracts - as distinct from the demand itself (scored in C3, Traction). It warrants its own weight because a company can have genuine government interest yet be unable to transact (no FCL, no ATO, no vehicle, no acquisition-literate personnel), and conversely a company can have strong transaction infrastructure ahead of large bookings. No other criterion captures transaction capability.
criterion.scope_note: SCOPE NOTE - C3 vs. C4: Awards, contracts, and revenue derived from government programs are scored in C3 (Product, Traction and Government Demand). Security clearances, facility clearances, authorizations (ATO/IL/FedRAMP/CMMC), ITAR/EAR registration, procurement vehicle eligibility, and program-office relationships are scored exclusively in C4 (Government Access and Procurement Pathway). An ATO grant is scored in C4 as an access credential; its resulting contract revenue is scored in C3. No single artifact or relationship is scored in both criteria.
criterion.band: Holds the full access stack required by the sub-sector: a Facility Clearance (FCL) and key-personnel clearances where classified work applies; a granted ATO/cATO or IL4-IL6 authorization (software); a Blue UAS listing (UAS); or a section 4022(f)-eligible production pathway (hardware). One or more documented program-office or contracting-officer relationships (named office, not rumored). Demonstrated pathway literacy (an executed contract vehicle - OTA/SBIR/IDIQ - plus acquisition-experienced personnel on the team). A-DELTA: at Profile A the authorization must be GRANTED/ACTIVE; at Profile B a credible IN-PROGRESS authorization (ATO underway with a sponsoring office) supports the top band.
At least one strong access signal (an executed vehicle OR an active clearance/authorization) but not the full stack. Program-office engagement evidenced but not yet a sustained, named relationship.

Demonstrates pathway awareness (talks the OTA/FAR/DFARS language, has a registered SAM.gov entity, ITAR/EAR registration where required) but lacks demonstrated relationships or authorizations. CMMC required-but-absent where the contract type will demand it is a scored deduction within this band, not a disqualifier.

No clearances, no authorizations, no SAM.gov registration, no documented government relationship; no evidence of pathway literacy. Absence of an ITAR/EAR registration where the product plainly requires it (flag).
criterion.regulatory_analog_scoring: REGULATORY-ANALOG SCORING (the defense "FDA-designation" analogs): - ATO (software): granted supports the top band; in-progress with a sponsoring office supports upper-mid. OPERATIVE-GATE TEST (required determination for software-primary companies): an ATO IS the operative gate when the product's delivery model requires the COMPANY to hold its own authorization to transact - cloud or SaaS delivered into a government boundary under the company's authorization. An ATO is NOT the operative gate when deployment inherits the CUSTOMER'S authorization boundary - on-premises, customer-deployed, offline/edge, or own-data architectures. The C4 Justification must state the operative-gate determination and its delivery-model basis. TREATMENT WHERE THE ATO IS THE OPERATIVE GATE AND NO ENGAGEMENT EXISTS: at Profile A, no ATO engagement caps C4 at the lower-mid ceiling (max 6); at Profile B, no ATO engagement is a WITHIN-BAND DEDUCTION, not a cap - a DECLARED PROFILE DELTA executing v1.0's inline soften condition, met twice in the first cohort (credible software companies transacting via non-ATO pathways at seed). Where the ATO is NOT the operative gate per the test, ATO absence carries no cap and no deduction. [TENTATIVE - the test's APPLIED path (a software company where the ATO clearly IS the operative gate) is untested in the first cohort; validate on first contact.] - FedRAMP: a stage-neutral strong signal wherever present (achievable at either profile; scored as a positive access signal, not tied to Profile A vs. B). - CMMC: absence where the contract type requires it is a scored deduction within the applicable band (not a disqualifier); presence is a modest positive supporting the upper-mid or top band. - ITAR/EAR registration: a BASELINE EXPECTATION. Its presence is not scored up; its absence where the product plainly requires it is a flag and contributes to the lowest band. (Adjudicated ITAR/EAR enforcement is separately the disqualifier A2.)
criterion.scored_sub_component: PROCUREMENT PATHWAY LITERACY (scored as position-within-band inside C4, never standalone). Positioning rule: - Demonstrated literacy (top of band): an EXECUTED contract vehicle (OTA/SBIR/IDIQ) AND acquisition-experienced personnel on the team (former contracting officer, PEO/program staff, or a founder with documented procurement experience). BOTH required. - Partial literacy (middle): EITHER an executed vehicle OR acquisition-experienced personnel, not both. - Nascent literacy (lower portion): SAM.gov-registered, references OTA/FAR/DFARS/SBIR correctly, but has no executed vehicle and no acquisition-experienced personnel - awareness without demonstrated capability. The C4 Justification must document the pathway-literacy position and the basis (executed vehicle? acquisition-experienced personnel?).
criterion.application_note: SOFTWARE APPLICATION NOTE: weight ATO/cATO/IL level and FedRAMP status as the primary access signals.

HARDWARE APPLICATION NOTE: weight FCL, type-classification/qualification pathway, and production-OT eligibility (section 4022(f)); ATO is generally not the operative gate (hardware companies are not capped on ATO).

criterion.name: Cap Table and Investor Base
criterion.revision_note: The CFIUS/FOCI concern spectrum is the primary scoring logic (Design Section 9A), implemented as explicit band ceilings. Trusted-capital definition per Design Section 9B; defense-prime CVC routing per Design Section 9C; four-tier syndicate hierarchy per Design Section 9D. Disqualifier-level CFIUS/FOCI is gated in Block 2 (A1) before scoring; this criterion scores only sub-disqualifier concern levels. Stage-invariant content. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the foreign-stake mitigable/unmitigable threshold, fund-tier membership, and operator-angel tier are calibration items.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates cap-table cleanliness and the quality of capital behind the company: CFIUS/FOCI exposure, trusted-capital sourcing, syndicate/lead quality, and defense-prime CVC dynamics. A messy or structurally compromised cap table, unmitigated FOCI, IP not assigned, stacked SAFEs above $3M with no priced round, and founder ownership below threshold are hard disqualifiers per Section 2.3.
