This criterion scores only sub-disqualifier CFIUS concern levels and syndicate quality.

band.label: Clean Cap Table, Trusted Capital, Specialist Lead

criterion.band: All-US / trusted-capital sources, no adversarial (PRC/Russia/Iran/DPRK/sanctioned-nexus) capital; NSIC-compatible. A Tier-1 specialist or institutional lead is in or near the round (see syndicate hierarchy: In-Q-Tel, a16z American Dynamism, Founders Fund, Lux, Shield Capital, Razor's Edge, 8VC, DCVC, General Catalyst defense practice). IP cleanly assigned to the company; no foreign-entity assignment; clean prior-round structure. PRECEDENCE NOTE: the Block-2 C1 gate governs the IP-assignment DETERMINATION; the "IP cleanly assigned" mention here is descriptive band content, not a second adjudication - where C1 is marked CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED, this dimension scores per Section 1.5 and the band mention neither re-triggers nor re-opens the gate.

Allied/friendly international investor present, OR a US fund with an opaque LP structure (defaults to moderate, not clean), OR a credible Tier-2 specialist lead rather than Tier-1. No disqualifying FOCI; any foreign nexus is allied and disclosed.

High-concern but sub-disqualifier CFIUS posture: known foreign-LP concentration in an investing fund, OR a CFIUS-mitigable foreign co-founder with a disclosed mitigation agreement (this caps the criterion at this lower-mid ceiling). Generalist VC with no defense thesis, or an operator-angel syndicate with no institutional lead.

Friends-and-family only / no lead; chaotic prior rounds; founder ownership already marginal (approaching the below-10%/below-15% disqualifier thresholds without crossing them). Undisclosed or evasive responses on capital sourcing (INFORMATION-ABSENT on a diligence-critical dimension).
criterion.cfius_foci_concern_spectrum:
CFIUS/FOCI CONCERN SPECTRUM (determines C5 band ceiling - this is the primary scoring logic, not a secondary note):
DISQUALIFIER LEVEL (Block 2 gate - not scored in C5): Unmitigated FOCI clearly blocking contract eligibility (foreign control without mitigation agreement; adversarial-state investor with board rights). Evaluated at Block 2 (Disqualifier A1); C5 is not scored.
HIGH-CONCERN / SUB-DISQUALIFIER (C5 capped at lower-mid ceiling): A US fund with KNOWN FOREIGN-LP CONCENTRATION that creates FOCI risk; OR a CFIUS-mitigable foreign co-founder with a DISCLOSED mitigation agreement. Cap: B5 max 5 / A5 max 5.
MODERATE CONCERN (C5 capped at upper-mid ceiling): Any ALLIED/FRIENDLY-NATION international investor (non-adversarial, non-controlling); OR an all-US fund whose LP structure is OPAQUE OR UNDISCLOSED. Opaque LP structures default to MODERATE - never to CLEAN. Cap: B5 max 7 / A5 max 8.
CLEAN (C5 top band eligible): All-US trusted-capital sources only, no adversarial nexus (no PRC-, Russia-, Iran-, DPRK-linked or sanctioned-entity capital, no adversarial sovereign fund), NSIC-compatible, LP structure visible or reasonably assessable as all-US.
TRUSTED-CAPITAL DEFINITION: US plus allied/friendly-nation capital with no adversarial nexus (no PRC-, Russia-, Iran-, DPRK-linked or sanctioned-entity capital, and no sovereign-fund capital from an adversarial state).
PUBLIC-SOURCE ASSESSMENT METHOD: Investor names and fund identities from Crunchbase/PitchBook/Business Wire; sovereign or PRC-linked fund names from known lists; NSIC/DFARS disclosures; press on any CFIUS review. An LP structure that cannot be assessed defaults to MODERATE concern (not clean) - the evaluator cannot certify cleanliness it cannot see.
FORWARD-LOOKING CFIUS FLAG (Block 5, not C5 scored): When foreign capital is currently tolerable but will become disqualifying once classified or greater-than-$5M unclassified work is pursued (the 2026 DFARS section 847 expansion from ~2,000 to ~41,000 reviewed companies), record a Block-5 CFIUS Forward-Looking Note. The note does not affect the C5 score; it documents the maturation risk.
The C5 Justification MUST state the assessed CFIUS concern level (disqualifier / high-concern / moderate / clean) and the basis.
criterion.cvc_routing_instruction: DEFENSE-PRIME CVC ROUTING (Lockheed Martin Ventures, RTX Ventures, Boeing/AEI HorizonX, Northrop, etc.): Positive strategic validation (pilot access, technical endorsement) is scored in C5 (Cap Table / investor quality). Acquirer-fit value (the prime as a plausible acquirer) is scored in C7-Exit (Design Section 10) - NEVER both (no double-count). Exclusivity / control / right-of-first-refusal terms that constrain independence are an independence deduction within C5 PLUS a Block-5 independence-concern flag.
criterion.syndicate_quality_hierarchy: SYNDICATE-QUALITY / SPECIALIST-LEAD HIERARCHY (scored specifically - generic VC presence is NOT credited; research Design-Risk #5). The evaluator MUST name the lead and its tier in the C5 Justification; crediting an unnamed "VC round" is a format error. - Tier 1 lead: In-Q-Tel; a16z American Dynamism; Founders Fund; Lux Capital; Shield Capital; Razor's Edge; 8VC; DCVC; General Catalyst defense practice. A Tier-1 lead or near-term term sheet supports the C5 top band. - Tier 2 lead: dedicated smaller defense specialists (Squadra, Decisive Point, Scout, Overmatch, Harpoon, Marlinspike, Silent, Snowpoint, Cubit, Ensemble) OR a top-tier generalist fund acting on an explicit defense thesis. Supports upper-mid. - Tier 3 lead: a generalist VC with NO defense thesis, OR an operator-angel syndicate (e.g., Elad Gil, Palmer Luckey, Delian Asparouhov, Trae Stephens as angels). Supports lower-mid. [TENTATIVE - some operator-angel leads may carry signal closer to Tier 2; calibrate.] - Tier 4: friends-and-family / no institutional lead. Lowest.

criterion.name: Capital Efficiency and Milestone Structure
criterion.revision_note: Defined separately for Profile A (burn vs. bookings and contract economics). Evaluates whether the company converts capital into milestone progress at a rate appropriate to defense revenue cycles, and whether non-dilutive capital is leverage rather than a substitute for real demand ("SBIR addiction"). Hardware/software application notes per Design Section 3. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the Seed runway threshold is a conventional venture default, not defense-specific primary data.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates whether the company converts capital into milestone progress at a rate appropriate to defense revenue cycles. At Series A, with revenue present, efficiency is read directly from burn against bookings and contract economics. The SBIR-addiction signature cross-references the C3 SBIR-progression deduction (Design Section 12B).
criterion.band: Burn well-covered by contracted backlog/bookings; favorable program economics; non-dilutive capital amplifies (not replaces) contract revenue; clear path to default-alive.
Burn reasonable against bookings; economics workable; minor concentration or margin concerns.
Burn high relative to bookings; thin program margins; runway dependent on the current raise closing.

Burn far exceeds bookings; no credible path to sustainable economics; SBIR-dependence persisting at Series A scale (cross-reference the C3 SBIR-progression deduction and Design Section 12B). ADDITIONAL NAMED FLOOR-BAND PATTERNS per B6: the FOUNDER-CAPITAL MULTI-YEAR STALL and the ZERO-DOCUMENTED-CAPITAL-HISTORY POSTURE (INFORMATION-ABSENT per Section 1.5's C6 deployment-evidence definition) score this band where they present at Profile A.
criterion.application_note: HARDWARE APPLICATION NOTE: capital intensity is structurally higher (tooling, materials, production lines); relax burn-multiple expectations and weight capital-efficiency-of-production instead (units or production-rate per dollar, demonstrated yield). A higher burn that is building manufacturing throughput is read as investment, not inefficiency - corroborate with the C7 "factory is the weapon" note. Invoke via the Block-1 hardware-intensive track tag; cite the tag and its assignment basis (fundability-physics rule per Block 0) in the C6 Justification.
SOFTWARE APPLICATION NOTE: standard burn-vs-revenue discipline applies; weight gross margin and deployment efficiency.

criterion.name: Competitive Position and Exit Optionality
criterion.revision_note: Moat and Exit are MERGED into a single criterion (Design Section 1 Decision 3) so the seven-criterion convention holds; each is a scored sub-component reconciled into one C7 band. Internal split is approximately Moat 7 / Exit 5 within A7=12 [TENTATIVE - analyst-assigned; calibrate if Exit proves more or less legible than assumed]. Moat hierarchy and patent treatment per Design Section 8; Exit acquirer universe and single-program-dependency cap per Design Section 10. Deliberately a low-weighted criterion at Seed, rising at Series A as throughput, sole-source positioning, and platform lock-in become assessable. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the internal Moat/Exit split, the throughput-vs-sole-source ordering, the hardware-patent magnitude, and the single-program hard-cap are all calibration items.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates competitive defensibility (Moat sub-component) and strategic-acquisition optionality (Exit sub-component) as a single combined read. The band reflects the COMBINED Moat-plus-Exit assessment; each sub-component is scored as position-within-band and reconciled into one C7 score. The lowest-weighted criterion at Seed by deliberate design (moat/exit are largely illegible early; the June 2026 Stephens shakeout warning makes venture multiples unreliable), rising at Series A.

band.label: Strong Defensibility and Clear Exit Optionality

criterion.band: A high-observability moat: platform lock-in with a PoR (Maven Smart System / Lattice integration), demonstrated manufacturing throughput ("the factory is the weapon"), or documented sole-source positioning (SAM.gov J and A). AND multiple credible strategic acquirers in the named universe plausibly fit the company's product and scale, with no single-program dependency and comparable transactions available to cite.

At least one credible moat type (a qualification/ATO/clearance barrier to entry, or emerging manufacturing throughput) AND a plausible (if narrower) acquirer set. Some concentration risk but not single-program-dependent.

Moat asserted but weakly observable; narrow or speculative acquirer fit. Single-program or single-customer dependency CAPS the Exit sub-component at this lower-mid ceiling, subject to the broad-universe exception in the Exit sub-component (see Exit sub-component, Design Section 10C).

No defensible position observable and no patents where they would be expected for the technology type (see Moat patent treatment, Design Section 8B); no credible acquirer path; commodity positioning; no comparable transactions.
criterion.scored_sub_component:
MOAT SUB-COMPONENT (scored as position-within-the-C7-band, reconciled with Exit; never a standalone number). Defense moat hierarchy, ordered strongest to weakest fundability signal AND weighted by observability (favor observable signals): 1. Platform lock-in with a PoR - integration into a funded DoD system (Maven Smart System, Lattice OS). Strongest AND highly observable; anchors the top. 2. Manufacturing / production-throughput advantage ("the factory is the weapon") - observable via facilities, production-rate disclosures, and delivery records. 3. Sole-source positioning - observable via SAM.gov sole-source justifications and J and A (Justification and Approval) documents. 4. ATO / clearance / qualification barriers to entry - the defense regulatory-moat analog; observable. 5. ITAR/EAR-protected technical know-how - strong in practice but largely INFORMATION-SCARCE. 6. Classified approaches - existence sometimes observable, details protected (INFORMATION-SCARCE). Top Moat positions require a high-observability moat (platform-lock-in-with-PoR, throughput, or sole-source). [TENTATIVE - the ordering of manufacturing throughput above sole-source positioning is a fundability judgment; calibrate against Series A-to-B outcomes.]
PATENT TREATMENT IN DEFENSE: - Software-primary defense companies: patents add approximately zero signal (carried from the Tech ICP treatment). - Hardware-intensive defense companies: patents add a modest positive signal (genuine barriers in manufacturing/materials/propulsion) - a within-band positioning nudge, not a band move [TENTATIVE - magnitude unquantified; set conservatively until cohort data exists]. - Absence of patents PLUS corroborated classified/ITAR work: NEUTRAL (treat as INFORMATION-SCARCE, not a weakness - patents would require disclosure the company cannot make). - Absence of patents PLUS no other moat PLUS no classified work: a genuine weakness contributing to the lowest C7 band.
SCARCE HANDLING FOR MOAT: ITAR-know-how and classified-approach moats are scored on the INFORMATION-SCARCE track - a corroborating artifact (a clearance/FCL signal, a USASpending obligation to a classified program office) supports a MIDPOINT Moat position with justification; a bare claim with no corroboration is INFORMATION-ABSENT (lowest). The Justification must name the corroborating artifact (Design Section 12A).
criterion.application_note: "THE FACTORY IS THE WEAPON" APPLICATION NOTE (Moat, hardware/manufacturing-intensive; Hadrian, X-Bow, Castelion archetype): demonstrated production rate, vertical integration, and facility scale SUBSTITUTE for an IP/patent moat. A company with a working high-throughput production line and vertical integration can reach the TOP of the Moat sub-component with little or no patent portfolio. Observable via facility announcements, production-rate disclosures, and delivery/units records. Invoke via the Block-1 hardware-intensive track tag; cite the tag and its assignment basis (fundability-physics rule per Block 0) in the C7 Justification. (Encodes the research finding that defense manufacturing investment rose to approximately $4.7B / 39 deals in 2025.)
SOFTWARE APPLICATION NOTE (Moat): patents add approximately zero signal; weight platform lock-in (PoR integration) and ATO/IL barriers to entry instead.
criterion.scored_sub_component:
EXIT SUB-COMPONENT (scored as position-within-the-C7-band, reconciled with Moat). PURPOSE: "The Exit sub-component measures the credibility and breadth of the company's strategic-acquisition optionality. It is deliberately underweighted because, at Seed, exit pathways are largely illegible, and because the June 2026 Stephens warning - venture-stage defense valuations of '50, 100, 200x' against a legacy industry trading at 2 to 2.5x revenue - makes exit-multiple-based scoring unreliable. The instrument therefore scores observable acquirer fit and single-program dependency, not speculative exit value."
NAMED STRATEGIC-ACQUIRER UNIVERSE (the only acquirers an evaluator may cite; no fabrication): Anduril (8-plus acquisitions, including ExoAnalytic); Palantir; L3Harris; RTX (Raytheon Technologies); Lockheed Martin; Northrop Grumman; Boeing; General Dynamics; SAIC; Leidos (acquired Kudu Dynamics for $300M in 2025); AeroVironment (acquired BlueHalo for approximately $4.1B enterprise value, 2024-2025).
EXIT POSITIONING: - TOP Exit position: MULTIPLE credible acquirers across the named universe plausibly fit the company's product and scale; NO single-program dependency; comparable transactions exist to cite. - UPPER-MID: a plausible acquirer set exists but is narrower; some concentration risk. - LOWER-MID: single-program dependency (one program/one customer drives the company) - this observable condition CAPS the Exit sub-component at the lower-mid ceiling, subject to the broad-universe exception below; narrow or speculative acquirer fit. - LOWEST: no credible acquirer path; commodity positioning; no comparable transactions.
COMPARABLE TRANSACTIONS an evaluator may cite for top/upper-mid placements: BlueHalo/AeroVironment (approximately $4.1B EV); Leidos-Kudu Dynamics ($300M, 2025); strategic buyers paying up to approximately 20x EBITDA for differentiated assets vs. approximately 2 to 2.5x revenue for the legacy defense industry.
SINGLE-PROGRAM-DEPENDENCY CAP (with broad-universe exception): When a company demonstrates single-program or single-customer dependency (one PoR, one contract vehicle, or one customer appears in all public records), this observable condition CAPS THE EXIT SUB-COMPONENT AT THE LOWER-MID CEILING within C7 - UNLESS the acquirer universe is demonstrably BROAD AND ACTIVE: MULTIPLE named acquirers from the permitted universe plausibly fit the company's product and scale AND a citable comparable transaction exists. When the exception applies, the dependency is a WITHIN-BAND DEDUCTION on the Exit sub-component rather than a hard cap. When the exception does NOT apply - concentrated demand WITHOUT a demonstrably broad courted universe, including the single-acquirer extension (only one plausible acquirer appears across the record) - the hard lower-mid cap stands. The cap-or-exception decision must cite the acquirer-universe breadth evidence either way (the named acquirers and the comp where the exception applies; the narrowness observation where it does not). [TENTATIVE - the exception executes the v1.0 inline soften condition, met once in the first cohort; the boundary between a broad and a narrow courted universe is a calibration item.]
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: For any TOP or UPPER-MID Exit position, the C7 Justification must NAME the candidate acquirers and CITE a comparable transaction. A top/upper-mid Exit placement without named acquirers and a cited comp is a format error.
VALUATION REALISM NOTE POINTER: Multiple-realism (any material gap between the company's implied raise valuation and the strategic-acquirer multiple universe) is recorded in the Block-5 Valuation Realism Note. It is QUALITATIVE ONLY, carries an explicit "not scored" annotation, and NEVER modifies the C7 score (additive-independence constraint). Do not route the valuation gap into the C7 score.

criterion.name: Team Quality and Defense-Domain Credibility
criterion.revision_note: Team is the single most heavily weighted criterion at Profile B (26 points, the highest weight in the instrument), reflecting that team is the dominant fundraising-velocity predictor at Seed (research Workstream 2b). NEAR-INVARIANT relative to A1: the halo_employer_taxonomy, Founder-Market-Fit sub-component, NCSP contradiction types, and INFORMATION-SCARCE/ABSENT treatment are IDENTICAL to A1 - refer to the A1 block for those elements. The two profile deltas: (1) the A1 top-band A-delta (prior exit or an executed government contract under this team) does NOT apply at Profile B - at Seed, exceptional teams routinely lack a prior exit or executed contract, so top-band placement is anchored on Tier-1 halo pedigree, complementary technical-plus-operational fit, and demonstrated development capacity; (2) the solo-founder deduction is 1 point at Profile B (vs. 2-3 at Profile A), reflecting that seed-stage specialists and operator-angels are more accepting of solo founders. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE per A1 revision_note.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the founding/executive team's demonstrated ability to build and field defense technology and to transact with the government, at the $500K-$3M Seed level. Measures the same blend as A1: (i) technical/engineering pedigree and (ii) operational/government-domain credibility (founder-market fit). At Seed, top-band signal is weighted toward Tier-1 defense halo pedigree and Founder-Market-Fit clarity rather than a prior exit. Single most important criterion at Profile B.
criterion.band: Per A1 top-band definition (Tier-1 defense halo employer in a role with real technical depth or program authority, OR a complementary Tier-1 technical-plus-operational pair; two or more FMF signals; demonstrated development capacity, not advisor-fronted; clearance-eligible/cleared key personnel where the domain requires it), WITH this Profile B adaptation: the A1 A-DELTA does NOT apply - a prior exit or an executed government contract is NOT required to anchor the top band at Seed. Top-band placement rests on Tier-1 halo pedigree, complementary technical-plus-operational fit, and demonstrated build capacity.

Per A1 upper-mid band definition (credible Tier-2 technical pedigree plus some domain credibility but missing EITHER elite technical depth OR deep operational/acquisition experience, OR strong Tier-2 coverage across both; one FMF signal; thin but demonstrated development capacity). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

Per A1 lower-mid band definition (relevant background thin on BOTH the technical-depth and operational-domain dimensions; FMF asserted via domain employment/education but no public artifacts, INFORMATION-SCARCE leads to midpoint within this band; no cleared personnel where the domain will require clearances). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

Per A1 lowest-band definition (no relevant defense-domain or elite-technical pedigree; the "advisor-heavy / engineering-light" Fool's-Gold pattern; founder identity/background uncorroborated by third-party sources, INFORMATION-ABSENT). Triggers NCSP review (Design Section 5D). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.
criterion.inherited_elements: The following A1 elements apply to B1 IDENTICALLY - refer to the A1 block: halo_employer_taxonomy (three credibility families, Tier-1/Tier-2 designations); scored_sub_component "Founder-Market Fit (FMF)" (earned-secret signal ladder, position-within-band scoring rule); negative_credibility_protocol (defense contradiction types, deduction magnitudes, documentation requirement, escalation of stolen-valor-grade fabrication to disqualifier D1). The Justification field must apply each of these exactly as specified for A1.
criterion.solo_founder_protocol: SOLO-FOUNDER TREATMENT (Profile B): apply a 1-point deduction within the assigned band for a solo founder. The reduced Profile B penalty (vs. Profile A's 2-3 points) reflects that seed-stage specialists and operator-angels are more accepting of solo founders. DEFENSE EXCEPTIONS (either waives the deduction): (1) a Tier-1 individual (former DARPA PM, senior PEO, senior SOF/IC leader) who has assembled a NAMED, CREDIBLE TECHNICAL BENCH; OR (2) a prior exit above $500M. DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: state the deduction (or waiving exception) and the resulting within-band position in the B1 Justification.

criterion.name: Sector and Market Alignment
criterion.revision_note: Stage-invariant content: the four-tier base sector classification, the 2025-2026 sector tier table, the SINGLE Sector Market-Event Modifier (plus/minus 2, single component - NOT split), the named-event requirement, the sector_tier_table_versioning staleness mechanism, and the OVC mechanism form are IDENTICAL to A2 - refer to the A2 block for the base-band sector lists, the full modifier value definitions, and the staleness mechanism. Only the point ranges and the OVC cap value differ. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE per A2 revision_note.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates whether the company operates in a defense sub-sector with active investor capital and downstream Series A appetite, at the Seed level. Uses the same structure as A2: a four-tier base classification (Tier 1 PEAK / Tier 2 ACTIVE / Tier 3 SELECTIVE / Out-of-Favor) plus a single Sector Market-Event Modifier (plus/minus 2), with the modifier as the sole envelope-expander.

band.label: Tier 1 PEAK Sub-Sector - Peak Investor Appetite

criterion.band: Per A2 top-band (Tier 1 PEAK) definition and the 2025-2026 sector tier table referenced there (e.g., autonomous systems / drones and counter-UAS, defense-AI / autonomy software, munitions and strike, space/ISR, maritime autonomy at peak appetite). Downstream Series A capital appetite is strong. No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

band.label: Tier 2 ACTIVE Sub-Sector - Active Investor Interest

criterion.band: Per A2 upper-mid band (Tier 2 ACTIVE) definition and the referenced tier table. Downstream Series A capital available; primary audience selectively deploys. No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

band.label: Tier 3 SELECTIVE Sub-Sector - Selective Investor Interest

criterion.band: Per A2 lower-mid band (Tier 3 SELECTIVE) definition and the referenced tier table. Downstream capital path is plausible but narrow. No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.
Per A2 lowest-band (Out-of-Favor) definition and the referenced tier table. Downstream Series A path is unclear or dependent on sector rotation. No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.
criterion.default_tier_rule: Per A2 default-tier rule, applied IDENTICALLY at Profile B: if the sub-sector is not on the dated tier table, default to Tier 3 / lower-mid (the Tier 3 SELECTIVE band at B2) and document the classification basis in the B2 Justification, including the table row(s) checked before the default was invoked. The precedence rule (explicit band criteria govern over the default) applies per A2. No Profile B adaptation. [v2.0 declared-delta removal: v1.0's B2 rule diverged undeclared from A2 (Tier 2 ACTIVE default; "unclassified" predicate); the divergence is removed and both profiles share A2's rule and predicate.]
criterion.sector_tier_table_versioning: Per A2 sector_tier_table_versioning (Design Section 12D): the tier table is the v2026-Q2 snapshot; when the analysis date is more than 12 months after the version date OR a mandatory trigger event has occurred since, stamp Block 0 and Block 5 with [SECTOR TIER TABLE STALE - v2026-Q2] and CAP the Sector Market-Event Modifier at plus/minus 1.

component.name: Sector Market-Event Modifier
component.status: Defense ICP v1.0 - single modifier (NOT split into multiple components)
component.instruction: Per A2 Component 1 (the SINGLE combined modifier - not split into two or three components). After assigning the base tier score, apply the modifier per the A2 value definitions. A modifier value other than 0 MUST cite a specific named event with a date in the B2 Justification; a non-zero modifier with no named event is a FORMAT ERROR. When the tier table is stale, cap this modifier at plus/minus 1.
component.modifier: Per A2 +2 definition (tens-of-billions sector-redefining appropriation; strategic acquisition with EV greater than $3B; flagship PoR anchoring the sub-sector; or a large Replicator/Drone-Dominance-scale procurement).
Per A2 +1 definition (a marquee sub-sector-specific appropriations increase; or a strategic acquisition in the $300M-$3B range).
Per A2 0 definition (no documented marquee event in the trailing window; the base tier score stands).
Per A2 -1 definition (a documented program cancellation or appropriations cut affecting the sub-sector; or a marquee down-round or shutdown of a comparable company).
Per A2 -2 definition (a sector-wide multiple compression or shakeout, the Stephens scenario; or a sub-sector-defining cancellation that resets appetite).

criterion.operational_viability_condition:
OPERATIONAL VIABILITY CONDITION (the "Fool's Gold" guard; mechanism form per A2, adapted for Profile B band thresholds).
TRIGGER: If the company scores in its lowest defined band on BOTH B1 (Team, Band 0-6) AND B3 (Product, Traction and Government Demand, Band 0-3 "Minimal or No Traction Evidence"), the B2 final score (base tier score plus any Sector Market-Event Modifier) is capped at the lower-mid ceiling (B2 max 9) AND the Sector Market-Event Modifier's positive range is suppressed (modifier maximum 0): no positive modifier may apply; an earned, named-and-dated NEGATIVE modifier still applies in full (the suppression binds positive modifiers only).
RATIONALE: Per A2 OVC rationale - when the company has neither a credible team nor any traction, a hot Tier-1 sub-sector score cannot be monetized. The anchors are C1 (Team) and C3 (Traction). The AND condition prevents penalizing a strong team with absent traction (or vice versa).
CAP VALUE: B2 capped at 9 (the lower-mid band ceiling); modifier maximum 0 (positive range suppressed; a documented negative modifier still applies).
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: When triggered, document the B1 and B3 scores, the uncapped B2 score, and the capped score recorded. When not triggered, a one-sentence confirmation suffices: "Operational Viability Condition not triggered - B1=[X] and/or B3=[X] above threshold."

criterion.name: Product, Traction and Government Demand
criterion.revision_note: Defined SEPARATELY for Profile B (pre-contract and early-award signals; content genuinely changes across stage). At Seed there is no ARR analog and typically no contract revenue; the signal-strength ladder runs from SBIR Phase I through DIU/AFWERX/NavalX OT and STRATFI/TACFI. The top band requires two or more strong signals (realistic, not aspirational). SBIR-Progression Quality (including the mill-signature deduction) is identical to A3 - refer to the A3 block. One of the two OVC anchors (with B1). EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the two-strong-signals top-band rule and the SBIR-mill numeric thresholds are analyst-set.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the maturity and credibility of the company's product and the strength of demonstrated government demand at the $500K-$3M Seed level. Pre-contract and early-award signals dominate; competitively-awarded non-dilutive funding and exercise demonstrations substitute for the absent ARR/contract-revenue signal. Signal-strength ladder (weakest to strongest): SBIR Phase I, then CRADA / early DARPA award, then a documented program-office relationship, then an exercise/wargame demonstration, then SBIR Phase II, then a DIU/AFWERX/NavalX OT prototype, then a STRATFI/TACFI award, then a Blue UAS listing (UAS-specific access gate).
criterion.scope_note: SCOPE NOTE - C3 vs. C4: Awards, contracts, and revenue derived from government programs are scored in C3 (Product, Traction and Government Demand). Security clearances, facility clearances, authorizations (ATO/IL/FedRAMP/CMMC), ITAR/EAR registration, procurement vehicle eligibility, and program-office relationships are scored exclusively in C4 (Government Access and Procurement Pathway). An ATO grant is scored in C4 as an access credential; its resulting contract revenue is scored in C3. No single artifact or relationship is scored in both criteria.
criterion.band: Two or more strong signals - e.g., SBIR Phase II PLUS a DIU OT; or a DIU OT PLUS a documented program-office relationship PLUS an exercise demonstration; or a STRATFI/TACFI award. A working prototype demonstrated in a military exercise/wargame (DS-3 or above).

ONE strong signal: SBIR Phase II, or a DIU/AFWERX/NavalX OT prototype, or a documented (not rumored) program-office relationship, or an exercise demonstration. A working prototype exists (DS-1 or above) and is on a credible transition path.
SBIR Phase I plus a prototype; or a CRADA; or a single early award without operational demonstration. Government interest evidenced but not yet competitively validated at the Phase II / OT level.

Concept only (DS-0): no government funding, no prototype, no program relationship. Marketing claims of "interest" with no SBIR.gov/USASpending corroboration (INFORMATION-ABSENT). This is the lowest B3 band and is one of the two OVC anchor conditions (with B1).
criterion.scored_sub_component: SBIR-PROGRESSION QUALITY: identical to the A3 sub-component - refer to the A3 block for the full positioning ladder (strong progression / healthy-in-progress / thin / mill signature) and the SBIR-MILL BEHAVIORAL DETECTION thresholds and deduction magnitudes [all TENTATIVE]. At Profile B, a thin progression (Phase I awards only, early, no Phase II yet) is consistent with stage and is NOT itself a mill signature; the mill-signature deduction applies only when the behavioral triggers are met. The adjudicated SBIR/FCA case remains the Block-2 B2 gate (superseding C3 scoring); the C3 mill deduction applies only to behavioral patterns without adjudication.
criterion.application_note: HARDWARE APPLICATION NOTE (counter-UAS kinetics, hypersonics, maritime hardware): ARR analogs do not apply; substitute contract backlog/bookings, units delivered/produced, demonstrated production rate (units/month), live-fire/qualification results, Blue UAS / type-classification status, and production-OT awards. At Seed, a successful live-fire demo plus an exercise demonstration substitutes for ARR at the top band. Invoke when Block 1 Market Context Note tags the company hardware-intensive; cite in the C3 Justification.

SOFTWARE APPLICATION NOTE (defense-AI, C4ISR, cyber): substitute ATO/IL trajectory, number of agency deployments/pilots, recurring contract value (where any exists), and integration onto a PoR platform (e.g., Maven Smart System, Lattice) for ARR. Invoke when Block 1 Market Context Note tags the company software-primary; cite in the C3 Justification.

criterion.name: Government Access and Procurement Pathway
criterion.status: Defense ICP v1.0 R4 - no predecessor analog
criterion.revision_note: Stage-invariant content: the band definitions, the regulatory_analog_scoring (ATO/FedRAMP/CMMC/ITAR-EAR), the Procurement Pathway Literacy sub-component, and both application notes are IDENTICAL to A4 - refer to the A4 block. The single profile delta is the authorization-maturity A-DELTA: at Profile A the authorization must be GRANTED/ACTIVE to anchor the top band; at Profile B a credible IN-PROGRESS authorization (an ATO underway with a sponsoring office) supports the top band. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE per A4 revision_note.
criterion.purpose: Government Access and Procurement Pathway measures the company's demonstrated capability to transact with the government - clearances, authorizations, program-office relationships, and acquisition-pathway literacy - as distinct from the demand itself (scored in C3). At Seed, a credible in-progress authorization (rather than a granted one) can anchor the top band. No other criterion captures transaction capability.
criterion.scope_note: SCOPE NOTE - C3 vs. C4: Awards, contracts, and revenue derived from government programs are scored in C3 (Product, Traction and Government Demand). Security clearances, facility clearances, authorizations (ATO/IL/FedRAMP/CMMC), ITAR/EAR registration, procurement vehicle eligibility, and program-office relationships are scored exclusively in C4 (Government Access and Procurement Pathway). An ATO grant is scored in C4 as an access credential; its resulting contract revenue is scored in C3. No single artifact or relationship is scored in both criteria.
criterion.band: Per A4 top-band definition (holds the full access stack required by the sub-sector: FCL and key-personnel clearances where classified work applies; ATO/cATO or IL4-IL6 for software; Blue UAS listing for UAS; or a section 4022(f)-eligible production pathway for hardware; one or more documented program-office/contracting-officer relationships; demonstrated pathway literacy), WITH this Profile B A-DELTA: a credible IN-PROGRESS authorization (an ATO underway with a sponsoring office) supports the top band at Seed - the authorization need not yet be GRANTED/ACTIVE as it must be at Profile A.

Per A4 upper-mid band definition (at least one strong access signal - an executed vehicle OR an active/in-progress clearance or authorization - but not the full stack; program-office engagement evidenced but not yet a sustained, named relationship). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range and the A-delta above.

Per A4 lower-mid band definition (pathway awareness - talks OTA/FAR/DFARS, SAM.gov-registered, ITAR/EAR registration where required - but lacks demonstrated relationships or authorizations; CMMC required-but-absent is a within-band scored deduction here, not a disqualifier). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

Per A4 lowest-band definition (no clearances, no authorizations, no SAM.gov registration, no documented government relationship, no evidence of pathway literacy; absence of ITAR/EAR registration where the product plainly requires it is a flag). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.
criterion.inherited_elements: The following A4 elements apply to B4 IDENTICALLY - refer to the A4 block: regulatory_analog_scoring (ATO granted/in-progress/absent treatment with the OPERATIVE-GATE TEST; where the ATO is the operative gate and no engagement exists, a lower-mid cap at Profile A and a WITHIN-BAND DEDUCTION at Profile B - a declared profile delta per the A4 text; FedRAMP as a stage-neutral strong signal; CMMC absence as a within-band deduction; ITAR/EAR registration as a baseline expectation); scored_sub_component "Procurement Pathway Literacy" (executed-vehicle-AND-acquisition-personnel positioning ladder); application_note Software-primary (ATO/cATO/IL and FedRAMP as primary access signals); application_note Hardware-intensive (FCL, type-classification/qualification, production-OT eligibility as primary access signals; ATO not the operative gate). The B4 Justification must document the pathway-literacy position and the assessed access stack exactly as specified for A4.

criterion.name: Cap Table and Investor Base
criterion.revision_note: Stage-invariant content: the CFIUS/FOCI concern spectrum (the primary scoring logic), the trusted-capital definition, the public-source assessment method, the defense-prime CVC routing, the four-tier syndicate hierarchy, and the Block-5 CFIUS Forward-Looking Flag are IDENTICAL to A5 - refer to the A5 block. Only the point ranges and the CFIUS band-ceiling values differ (at Profile B, high-concern caps at B5 max 5 and moderate caps at B5 max 7). Disqualifier-level FOCI is gated in Block 2 (A1) before scoring. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE per A5 revision_note.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates cap-table cleanliness and the quality of capital behind the company at the Seed level: CFIUS/FOCI exposure, trusted-capital sourcing, syndicate/lead quality, and defense-prime CVC dynamics. A messy or structurally compromised cap table, unmitigated FOCI, IP not assigned, stacked SAFEs above $3M with no priced round, and founder ownership below threshold are hard disqualifiers per Section 2.3. This criterion scores only sub-disqualifier CFIUS concern levels and syndicate quality.

band.label: Clean Cap Table, Trusted Capital, Specialist Lead

criterion.band: Per A5 top-band definition (all-US / trusted-capital sources, no adversarial nexus, NSIC-compatible; a Tier-1 specialist or institutional lead in or near the round - In-Q-Tel, a16z American Dynamism, Founders Fund, Lux, Shield Capital, Razor's Edge, 8VC, DCVC, General Catalyst defense practice; IP cleanly assigned; clean prior-round structure). At Profile B a clean SAFE-based or priced-seed structure is normal and fully top-band-eligible. CLEAN CFIUS posture required for this band.

Per A5 upper-mid band definition (allied/friendly international investor present, OR a US fund with an opaque LP structure defaulting to moderate, OR a credible Tier-2 specialist lead rather than Tier-1; no disqualifying FOCI). This is the MODERATE-concern CFIUS ceiling: B5 capped at 7 when concern is moderate (allied/non-controlling foreign investor, or opaque/undisclosed all-US LP structure).

Per A5 lower-mid band definition (generalist VC with no defense thesis, or an operator-angel syndicate with no institutional lead). This is the HIGH-CONCERN sub-disqualifier CFIUS ceiling: B5 capped at 5 when a US fund has KNOWN FOREIGN-LP CONCENTRATION creating FOCI risk, OR a CFIUS-mitigable foreign co-founder has a DISCLOSED mitigation agreement.

Per A5 lowest-band definition (friends-and-family only / no lead; chaotic prior rounds; founder ownership already marginal, approaching but not crossing the below-10%-post-Seed disqualifier threshold; undisclosed or evasive responses on capital sourcing, INFORMATION-ABSENT on a diligence-critical dimension). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.
criterion.inherited_elements: The following A5 elements apply to B5 IDENTICALLY - refer to the A5 block, substituting the Profile B band ceilings (high-concern → B5 max 5; moderate → B5 max 7): cfius_foci_concern_spectrum (disqualifier / high-concern / moderate / clean levels, the trusted-capital definition, the public-source assessment method with opaque-defaults-to-moderate, and the Block-5 CFIUS Forward-Looking Flag); cvc_routing_instruction (validation → C5, acquirer-fit → C7-Exit never both, exclusivity → C5 deduction plus Block-5 flag); syndicate_quality_hierarchy (Tier-1/Tier-2/Tier-3/Tier-4 lead quality; name the lead and tier or it is a format error). The B5 Justification MUST state the assessed CFIUS concern level and name the lead and its tier.

criterion.name: Capital Efficiency and Milestone Structure
criterion.revision_note: Defined SEPARATELY for Profile B (runway and non-dilutive leverage; content genuinely changes across stage). At Seed, efficiency is read from runway length and whether non-dilutive capital (SBIR/STTR/STRATFI/DARPA) is genuine leverage alongside a real demand signal, rather than from burn-against-bookings. The "SBIR-addiction signature" - grants as the ONLY revenue with no transition path - is the lowest-band marker and cross-references the C3 SBIR-progression deduction. Hardware/software application notes per Design Section 3. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE: the 18-24 month Seed runway threshold is a conventional venture default, not defense-specific primary data.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates whether the company converts capital into milestone progress at a rate appropriate to defense revenue cycles, at the Seed level. Reads runway length, milestone discipline, and whether non-dilutive capital amplifies a real demand signal or substitutes for one. The SBIR-addiction signature cross-references the C3 SBIR-progression deduction (Design Section 12B).
criterion.band: Lean burn with approximately 18-24 months runway at the target raise; non-dilutive capital (SBIR/STTR/STRATFI/DARPA) used as genuine leverage alongside a real demand signal. A milestone plan tied to value-inflecting events (Phase I to Phase II, prototype to production-OT, ATO grant).
Reasonable burn/runway; some non-dilutive capital; a milestone plan that is credible but has gaps.
Short runway or high burn for stage; non-dilutive capital present but not clearly tied to milestones; early signs of SBIR-reliance.

SBIR-ADDICTION SIGNATURE: non-dilutive grants are the ONLY revenue with no transition path (cross-reference the C3 SBIR-progression deduction and Design Section 12B); unsustainable burn; no milestone discipline. ADDITIONAL NAMED FLOOR-BAND PATTERNS (same band, distinct signatures): FOUNDER-CAPITAL MULTI-YEAR STALL - founder or friends-and-family capital sustaining years of activity with no external validation event and no milestone conversion; ZERO-DOCUMENTED-CAPITAL-HISTORY POSTURE - no capital history documented AND no corroborated deployment evidence (INFORMATION-ABSENT per Section 1.5's C6 deployment-evidence definition; scores this floor band, not a midpoint).
criterion.application_note: HARDWARE APPLICATION NOTE: capital intensity is structurally higher (tooling, materials, production lines); relax burn-multiple expectations and weight capital-efficiency-of-production instead (units or production-rate per dollar, demonstrated yield). A higher burn that is building manufacturing throughput is read as investment, not inefficiency - corroborate with the C7 "factory is the weapon" note. Invoke via the Block-1 hardware-intensive track tag; cite the tag and its assignment basis (fundability-physics rule per Block 0) in the C6 Justification.
SOFTWARE APPLICATION NOTE: standard burn-vs-revenue discipline applies; weight gross margin and deployment efficiency.

criterion.name: Competitive Position and Exit Optionality
criterion.revision_note: Stage-invariant content: the combined Moat-plus-Exit band logic, the defense moat hierarchy, the patent treatment, the "factory is the weapon" application note, the SCARCE handling, the named acquirer universe, the single-program-dependency cap, and the Block-5 Valuation Realism Note pointer are IDENTICAL to A7 - refer to the A7 block. Only the point ranges and the internal Moat/Exit split differ: within B7=8 the split is approximately Moat 5 / Exit 3 (vs. Moat 7 / Exit 5 within A7=12) [TENTATIVE - analyst-assigned]. The lowest-weighted criterion at Seed by deliberate design. EVIDENCE BASE IS TENTATIVE per A7 revision_note.
criterion.purpose: Evaluates competitive defensibility (Moat sub-component) and strategic-acquisition optionality (Exit sub-component) as a single combined read at the Seed level. The band reflects the COMBINED Moat-plus-Exit assessment. Deliberately the lowest-weighted criterion: moat and exit are largely illegible at Seed, and the June 2026 Stephens shakeout warning makes venture multiples unreliable.

band.label: Strong Defensibility and Clear Exit Optionality

criterion.band: Per A7 top-band definition (a high-observability moat: platform lock-in with a PoR, demonstrated manufacturing throughput, or documented sole-source positioning; AND multiple credible strategic acquirers in the named universe with no single-program dependency and comparable transactions to cite). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range and the Moat-5/Exit-3 internal split.

Per A7 upper-mid band definition (at least one credible moat type - a qualification/ATO/clearance barrier, or emerging manufacturing throughput - AND a plausible if narrower acquirer set; some concentration risk but not single-program-dependent). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

Per A7 lower-mid band definition (moat asserted but weakly observable; narrow or speculative acquirer fit; single-program/single-customer dependency CAPS the Exit sub-component at this lower-mid ceiling). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.

Per A7 lowest-band definition (no defensible position observable and no patents where they would be expected for the technology type; no credible acquirer path; commodity positioning; no comparable transactions). No Profile B adaptation beyond point range.
criterion.inherited_elements: The following A7 elements apply to B7 IDENTICALLY - refer to the A7 block, substituting the Profile B internal split (Moat approximately 5 of 8, Exit approximately 3 of 8): scored_sub_component "Moat (Defensibility)" (the six-type defense moat hierarchy ordered by strength and observability; the patent treatment - software approximately zero, hardware modest positive, no-patents-plus-classified neutral, no-patents-no-moat-no-classified a lowest-band weakness; the INFORMATION-SCARCE vs. ABSENT handling); application_note "factory is the weapon" (Hardware-intensive, Moat); application_note Software-primary (Moat); scored_sub_component "Exit (Acquirer Fit and Optionality)" (the named strategic-acquirer universe, the exit positioning ladder, the comparable transactions, the single-program-dependency cap with its broad-universe exception, and the Block-5 Valuation Realism Note pointer labeled "not scored"). The B7 Justification must NAME candidate acquirers and CITE a comparable transaction for any top/upper-mid Exit position, exactly as required for A7.

section.name: Standardized Scoring Output Format
section.revision_note: Output format inherits the seven-block structure from Tech ICP v1.0 / LS v5.1 with defense-specific field-level additions placed INTO existing blocks (no new blocks; Block IDs 0-6 only). Block 0 Sector field uses the defense four-part format (Tier / Sub-Sector / Software-vs-Hardware Track / Tier-Table Version) plus a [SECTOR TIER TABLE STALE] stamp field. Block 1 replaces the development-stage enumerated list with the DDST DS-0 through DS-7 taxonomy, adds the Stealth-Mode flag, and adds the four defense Market Context Note format strings. Block 2 replaces the ten-disqualifier four-category structure with the defense fourteen-disqualifier five-category structure (A-E). Block 3 modifier_sub_block carries ONE modifier component (Sector Market-Event Modifier, plus/minus 2; not three) and adds defense documentation requirements. Block 4 uses defense weight values and labels the OVC anchors C1 and C3. Block 5 uses the Defense Investor Archetype Taxonomy (seven archetypes) and adds the Valuation Realism Note, CFIUS Forward-Looking Flag, and Dual-Use Focus-Risk Note. Block 6 adds the defense Format Compliance items and the tier-table version stamp.

block.instruction: Header metadata for every evaluation. The Sector field uses the defense four-part format.

block.name: Disqualifier Screen
block.instruction: Screen all fourteen disqualifiers in five categories (A-E) per Section 2.3 BEFORE any scoring. Mark each CLEAR, TRIGGERED (with explanation), NOT APPLICABLE (where the non-applicability rule applies; marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification), or CONTINGENT - ATTESTATION REQUIRED (where a gate's contingent disposition applies per Section 2.3 - contingent marks do not disqualify and do not block scoring). If any disqualifier is TRIGGERED, the evaluation terminates: Blocks 3-5 are populated with "N/A - Disqualified" and the basis (EXCEPTION: the Block-4 Overall Data Confidence field is UNCONDITIONAL and is populated on every evaluation, including terminated and disqualified ones); Block 6 is still completed. A score below 40 with no disqualifier triggered is Tier 4 - Not Ready, NOT Out of Scope.

category.name: A - National Security and Export Control
category.field: [CLEAR / TRIGGERED - explanation. TRIGGERED only when foreign ownership/control/influence clearly blocks contract eligibility with NO disclosed mitigation agreement. A disclosed CFIUS mitigation agreement or allied/non-controlling capital is NOT this gate - it is a scored C5 concern (high or moderate). Sub-threshold CFIUS concern is recorded in C5 band ceilings.]

[CLEAR / NOT APPLICABLE / TRIGGERED - explanation. TRIGGERED only on a finalized/adjudicated export-control enforcement action (civil penalty, consent agreement, or criminal conviction - the Vescent Photonics archetype). An ITAR/EAR registration gap or open inquiry without adjudication is NOT this gate (it is a C4 lowest-band flag). Mark NOT APPLICABLE where the product plainly does not implicate ITAR/EAR.]

[CLEAR / NOT APPLICABLE / TRIGGERED - explanation. TRIGGERED only when an FCL is revoked/suspended AND the company's core revenue requires the now-blocked classified work (BOTH conditions). TWO-LEVEL TREATMENT (state explicitly): an ADJUDICATED finding is THIS Block-2 gate; a BEHAVIORAL SBIR-MILL PATTERN with no adjudication is NOT this gate - it is a SCORED DEDUCTION within C3 (Design Section 12B). data_confidence.instruction: Aggregate the per-criterion Data Confidence Flags into an overall rating. Apply the founder-attestation aggregation rule per Section 1.5: when two or more criteria carry INFORMATION-SCARCE flags driven by founder-attestation-only signals, the rating moves to MODERATE; when four or more, to LOW. This applies in parallel to the total INSUFFICIENT DATA flag count below. SPECIES-DISTINCT COUNTING: the aggregation counts INFORMATION-SCARCE and INFORMATION-ABSENT flags as DISTINCT SPECIES, and the rating must state both counts (e.g., "LOW - 6 flags: 2 SCARCE / 4 ABSENT"). ABSENT-DOMINATED ANNOTATION (required): when ABSENT flags are the majority of the count, the rating MUST carry the annotation that it reflects HIGH-CONFIDENCE EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE - the conclusions are reliable findings that the underlying activities do not exist, not thin-evidence uncertainty; the label without this annotation misstates the evaluation's epistemic character. GOVERNS-RULE: the mechanical flag-count ladder GOVERNS the label. A qualitative-override annotation (with its basis documented) may be recorded ALONGSIDE the ladder-governed label; it never replaces it. UNCONDITIONAL FIELD: every evaluation - including terminated, disqualified, and partial evaluations - carries an Overall Data Confidence rating; "N/A - Disqualified" is not a permitted value for this field.
data_confidence.rating: Two or fewer INSUFFICIENT DATA flags across all criteria; primary evidence is independently observable. Founder-attestation aggregation rule not triggered.

Three to five INSUFFICIENT DATA flags across criteria, OR the founder-attestation aggregation rule is triggered at the 2-criterion threshold. Some scores rest on midpoint-default or founder-attested bands; conclusions are directionally reliable but specific score points are less precise.

Six or more INSUFFICIENT DATA flags across criteria, OR the founder-attestation aggregation rule is triggered at the 4-criterion threshold. Many scores rest on midpoint-default or attested bands; conclusions are directionally indicative but should be confirmed before client-engagement decisions. (Common for legitimate-opsec stealth and classified-program-heavy companies; not by itself a negative signal.)
data_confidence.field: [HIGH / MODERATE / LOW with brief explanation citing the species-distinct flag counts (SCARCE vs ABSENT), any founder-attestation aggregation rule invocation, the ABSENT-dominated annotation where required, and any qualitative-override annotation recorded alongside the ladder-governed label. UNCONDITIONAL: populated for terminated and disqualified evaluations as well.]

operational_viability_summary.instruction: Summarize operational viability per the C1 (Team) and C3 (Traction) score bands. This applies regardless of whether the OVC formally triggered (the OVC trigger is the extreme case of the broader profile). The anchors are C1 and C3. The four labels below PARTITION all sixteen anchor-band geometries (four bands per anchor): OPERATIONAL covers both anchors in top or upper-mid (4 geometries); DEVELOPING covers at least one anchor in lower-mid with neither in lowest (5); MARGINAL covers exactly one anchor in lowest (6); PRE-OPERATIONAL covers both in lowest (1). Every evaluation maps to exactly one label, and the label selection must cite BOTH anchor band assignments.

mapping_rules.mapping: Both C1 (A1/B1) and C3 (A3/B3) are in their top or upper-mid bands. The company has demonstrated both team viability and government-demand validation. The fundraising path is unobstructed at the operational-viability level; success depends on sub-sector tier, market timing, and deal mechanics.

At least one of C1 (A1/B1) and C3 (A3/B3) is in its lower-mid band, and NEITHER is in its lowest band. The company has partially demonstrated both operational-viability dimensions: neither has failed, but at least one is not yet validated at the upper-mid level. The fundraising path is open but development-stage-conditional; the under-validated dimension(s) are documented in Top 3 Fundability Risks where material. The OVC has not triggered. This label covers the five anchor-band geometries previously uncovered between OPERATIONAL and MARGINAL.

C1 OR C3 (exactly one of the two) is in its lowest band. The company has demonstrated one of the two operational-viability dimensions but not the other. The path is conditional on remediation of the weak dimension. The OVC has not triggered (single condition); the asymmetric profile is flagged in Top 3 Fundability Risks.

Both C1 AND C3 are in their lowest defined bands. The Operational Viability Condition has triggered and C2 is capped at the lower-mid ceiling (A2 at 7 / B2 at 9) with the modifier's positive range suppressed (modifier maximum 0; a documented negative modifier still applies). The company has demonstrated neither minimum operating capacity nor minimum government-demand validation; the fundraising path is structurally obstructed regardless of sub-sector tailwinds.

fundraising_outlook.instruction: Synthesizes the evaluation into a forward-looking narrative: (a) the most likely investor archetype that will lead the round; (b) the expected timeline and process dynamics; (c) the key risks to closing. The Most Likely Investor Archetype is selected from the Defense Investor Archetype Taxonomy below. A primary archetype is required; a secondary is optional when two distinct paths are visible.

defense_investor_archetypes.archetype: A Tier-1 specialist fund leading the round (a16z American Dynamism, Founders Fund defense vertical, Lux Capital, 8VC, DCVC, General Catalyst defense practice). Writes $2M-$15M-plus checks across Seed and Series A. Primary fit signals: defense/dual-use sector classification, elite founding-team pedigree (Anduril/Palantir/DARPA/DIU alumni), government contract traction, CFIUS-clean cap table. Best fit: Tier-1/Tier-2 sub-sector companies with strong team and demonstrated government demand, either profile.

In-Q-Tel and equivalent IC/strategic capital vehicles (OSC, APFIT, NSIC, equivalent). Provides non-equity or equity-adjacent investment with catalytic downstream validation (for every dollar IQT invests, approximately $28-$40 of commercial VC typically follows). Primary fit signals: IC/government-validated problem urgency, technology transition/adoption readiness. Best fit: companies whose problem has explicit IC/operational urgency and a transition path.

Dedicated defense seed specialists writing first institutional checks at $250K-$5M (Squadra Ventures, Scout Ventures, Decisive Point, Harpoon Ventures, Silent Ventures, Overmatch Ventures, Marlinspike Partners, Snowpoint Ventures, Cubit Capital, Ensemble VC). Often leads before Tier-1 institutional funds engage. Primary fit signals: strong team signal in a Tier-1/Tier-2 sub-sector, early government demand (Phase I / exercise demo), CFIUS-clean. Best fit: Profile B companies with strong team and emerging government traction.

CVC arms of major defense primes (Lockheed Martin Ventures, expanding toward approximately $1B; RTX Ventures; Boeing/AEI HorizonX; Northrop Grumman; Booz Allen; L3Harris strategic capital). Provides GTM access, pilot partnerships, and a potential acquirer signal. Independence caveats apply (exclusivity/control terms - a C5 deduction plus a Block-5 flag). Primary fit signals: alignment with the prime's technology roadmap, supply-chain fit, absence of CFIUS/FOCI complications. Best fit: companies whose product fits a prime's roadmap and whose cap table can absorb a strategic without independence concerns.

Individual operator-angels and their co-investment syndicates (Elad Gil, Palmer Luckey, Delian Asparouhov, Trae Stephens, and comparable operators). Typically lead at pre-seed or early seed at $100K-$2M. Often a precursor to institutional defense rounds. Primary fit signals: founder-pedigree alignment with the angel's domain, a compelling technology thesis. Best fit: early Profile B companies with strong founder credibility ahead of institutional traction.

A top-tier generalist fund acting on an explicit defense or national-security thesis (not merely defense-sector-aware). Writes $3M-$15M checks. Primary fit signals: strong founding team with crossover appeal (commercial plus defense), dual-use positioning, Tier-1/Tier-2 sub-sector, institutional-quality cap table. Best fit: Profile A companies with crossover team appeal and dual-use optionality.

SBIR/STTR (Phase I/II/III), STRATFI/TACFI, DIU/AFWERX/NavalX OT, DARPA grants, OSC/APFIT/NSIC. Not equity; non-dilutive validation capital that reduces burn and provides a demand signal.
